title: The worst airline I've ever tried
text:

title: Horrible Experience with Air India – Cost Me £2480 FOR £926 regular ticket
text:
I booked my flight a month ago to avoid any last-minute issues, but Air India changed my flight timings three times before my actual travel date. Then, just one hour before departure, they canceled my flight via email, leaving me stranded with no proper alternative.

They rebooked me for a flight the next day, but it had a 16-hour layover for a simple domestic connection, which was completely unreasonable. With help from my travel agency, I managed to change it to a better option, but I had to pay an extra £46 just to reschedule.

Unfortunately, due to an Elizabeth Line failure, I missed my flight the next day. I immediately went to the Air India reception desk at the airport, where the staff initially said they would help. Instead, they wasted 30 minutes of my time, only to tell me at the end that I was a "no-show" and that all my remaining tickets were canceled.

To make matters worse, the flight didn’t even depart on time—it left 45 minutes late. So after all the stress they put me through, it turns out the flight wasn’t even punctual.

Now, Air India doesn’t even pick up my calls, making it impossible to get any resolution. Despite explaining my situation and requesting a rebooking or at least a partial refund, they refused to assist in any way. In the end, I only received £13 back from my £926 ticket, and I had to pay £1,500 for a last-minute replacement flight.

Their customer service is unprofessional, dismissive, and completely unhelpful. Instead of assisting a stranded passenger, they chose to do nothing.

I will never book with Air India again and strongly advise others to choose a more reliable airline that values its passengers and provides genuine customer support.

title: 10 out of 30 Business class seats on 15-hour flight not recling/operable
text:
Air India - A Disastrous Experience That No Traveler Should Endure

I am beyond frustrated with the appalling service I received from Air India during my business class flight from Delhi to Toronto on November 30, 2024. This was supposed to be a luxurious, relaxing journey in business class, courtesy of my Aeroplan reward ticket. However, what I encountered was nothing short of a nightmare.

Just before boarding the 15-hour flight, I was informed that the flat-bed seat in business class wouldn’t recline. To make matters worse, 10 other business class seats were also broken. Out of 30+ business class seats, nearly a third were non-operational! How is this aircraft even allowed to fly with such issues? Isn’t someone at the Directorate General of Civil Aviation supposed to ensure safety and service standards?

Despite this, Air India refused to endorse my ticket to another carrier, and I had no choice but to endure a 15-hour flight with a business class ticket, but NO business class comfort. It was an uncomfortable, miserable journey, not what I paid for or expected. But it didn’t end there.

Upon arrival, Air India promised a firm upgrade voucher and claimed that Air Canada would refund my Aeroplan miles. Six weeks and 10 emails later, I finally received the voucher. But what good is it? When I called the call center to inquire about using it, I was told that I would have to present it at the airport to be considered for an upgrade. What if business class is full? Will I be stuck flying in economy AGAIN? And no one at the call center could even tell me whether I should carry business class baggage (2 x 32kg) or economy class baggage (2 x 23kg).

The entire experience was a disaster. Air India’s lack of professionalism, miscommunication, and sheer disregard for customer service has left me with zero trust in this airline. This is NOT how business class travelers should be treated.

Air India, you owe me a full apology, proper compensation, and a commitment to never let this happen to another passenger. If anyone is considering flying with them, BE WARNED.

title: Privatization has only made Air India WORSE than it already was

Air India had a notorious reputation as a government owned enterprise. Hopes were high when it got privatized a couple of years ago. However, the service has actually deteriorated further. Regardless of the class of service -- Business, Premium Economy or Economy -- my parents (and I) have, on multiple occasions, regretted giving our patronage to this airline. Some examples of the horrors of dealing with this airline *after its privatization* are as follows:
- MAINTENANCE: Business class seating had functional issues (movie screen not working, recliner not working etc.) on 17 hour international flights, and, despite raising it with the staff, NOTHING WAS DONE during the flight - even a seat change was not possible. My parents had to continue in the defective seats, without any reprieve. Attempts at grievance resolution through customer support, after the flight, went nowhere. You can always expect to be on hold on the phone for hours at end, passed around from one agent to another, and so on, when grievance resolution is involved. If this wasn't enough, my parents faced the same issue even on the return flight! Bear in mind these were 17 hour international flights that faced this issue.
- SCHEDULING: We didn't learn our lesson the first time. We regrettably booked by Air India again due to unavailability of other options, and because the airline recently upgraded its airline fleet between DEL<-->SFO. So, keeping our fingers crossed, I went ahead with the booking. What started then was an almost non-stop sequence of schedule changes, cabin class downgrades etc, that continued for weeks, for multiple reservations. Ultimately, I decided to cancel the flights, since cabin downgrades an schedule changes (>3 hours) entitle travelers to cancel their tickets without a penalty (full refund) based on US DOT regulations. But, even for this, one has to first be able to reach the airline, which was essentially impossible. After multiple calls to the travel agent, and again being put on hold for hours, the situation went nowhere, and I ultimately had to dispute the charge on my credit card statement. Nothing seems to work with this airline other than force or legal escalation. Gone are the days when Air India felt like "our" airline, as Indians.
- CONNECTIONS/TRANSIT: I recently also faced an issue with a missed connection, with the airline trying to penny-pinch even their obligation to provide you with a comfortable transit while you wait for the next connecting flight. I had to raise hell to be allowed to even use the Air India lounge while I waited for an alternative connecting flight after a missed connection caused by Air India, when transiting in BOM during my SFO --> GOI journey.

Expect hours of frustration at some point or other, when you book with this airline. They bait you with good pricing, and the shortest travel routes between the US and India, but beware that you will "pay" for it in other intangible ways, more than what you think you might save in the short-term. I personally don't plan to ever use Air India again. Booking the ticket is just one part of an overall travel experience. There is the seating itself (which may not be functional), flight and schedule changes (during the days leading upto the flight), delayed flights (while you travel), horrendous treatment enroute (if you are stranded between connections due to those delays), protracted grievance resolution process (after the journey), and almost always an unacceptably large investment of your time dealing with the airline for any and all of the above. Literally none of my, or my parents', overall journeys on this airline since it went private have been pleasant.

Furthermore, three of my friends, who were also flying with Air India, encountered similar issues with their flights being disrupted and having to call to change their bookings.

Extremely Disappointing Experience with Air India – Poor Check-In Process

I traveled with Air India on July 13th from Delhi Airport (7 AM international check-in), and my experience was nothing short of a nightmare. The ordeal started with the first staff member assisting us. We essentially completed the check-in process, but due to some confusion over a bag tag and the manager’s remarks about a “roller,” the entire check-in was canceled. To make things worse, the manager either went on lunch or ended his shift, leaving us stranded for 15 minutes.

Then, Shashi Kant arrived, and the chaos continued for another 45 minutes. He didn’t initially ask for my visa, but I proactively mentioned it. He started interrogating me about my stay, trip duration, and flight details for my return home, despite me being a U.S. citizen and Maldives not requiring a visa. Why does any of this matter to Air India?

To add to the frustration, my luggage was a few kilograms over the limit, but it was our honeymoon, and when traveling from any country to India, there’s usually some leniency. However, the staff refused to accommodate us, and even their manager denied our request. I had to pay for the extra weight, but the process was a mess. The lady handling payments didn’t even know the correct charges. She used her personal iPhone for assistance, charged $17 per kg without announcing the amount beforehand, and barely explained anything. Instead, she kept talking on the phone and wasted another 15 minutes.

The total time at check-in? A staggering 1 hour and 15 minutes. This is completely unacceptable. The inefficiency, lack of proper training, and unprofessional behavior reflect poorly on Air India.

I urge the airline to reinvest in its staff, provide proper training, and benchmark against international standards. Sending staff to other countries to see how a seamless check-in process works might help improve the overall experience.

title: Disappointing Experience with Air India Flight Vouchers on Credit Cards after Vistara merger with Air India
text:
If you're considering getting a credit card from Axis, SBI, or any other issuer that offers Air India flight vouchers as a benefit, I strongly recommend reconsidering. Here's why:

Lack of Seat Availability:
I’m planning a trip from Delhi to Leh in February, but Air India doesn’t have flights available till March. I even tried to check flights from Delhi to Bagdogra, and again, they don’t have any flights till March. Air India seems to have almost no seat availability on any route if you're trying to book 3–4 months before your travel date. This makes the vouchers practically useless, especially if you're planning a trip in advance.

Decline in Service Post-Merger:
Before the merger with Air India, Vistara provided a much better experience for voucher redemptions. You could easily secure flights even if you booked just a month in advance. The ease of booking, availability of seats, and the overall service were far superior. The stark difference in service quality is evident post-merger.

Wasted Benefits:
I’ve been holding two credit cards (Axis+SBI) for the past five years, and right now, I have four unused vouchers because I can't find any flights to redeem them on. It’s frustrating to pay for credit card benefits that you can't actually utilize.

Conclusion:
Avoid credit cards that offer Air India flight vouchers unless the airline drastically improves its seat availability and redemption process. The perks may look attractive on paper, but in reality, they’re more trouble than they’re worth. Save your money and invest in cards that offer more reliable and usable benefits.

Tip for Banks:
Reconsider partnerships and ensure that your customers can actually use the benefits you're promoting. Otherwise, it reflects poorly on your brand too.

title: Air India: The Worst Airline Experience of My Life – 150 Lost Suitcases and Zero Help
text:
I honestly don’t even know where to begin with just how horrific my experience with Air India was. It was a total disaster from start to finish.

Let’s start with the fact that Air India managed to lose 150 suitcases on my flight from London Heathrow to Mumbai. That’s right – 150! And guess what? Many of those suitcases didn’t even make it onto the plane in the first place, despite receiving confirmation emails from Air India that my baggage was checked in and loaded. We found out about this catastrophic screw-up only after we landed in Mumbai – absolutely no communication before then.

When we arrived at Mumbai Airport, the chaos was like something out of a nightmare. There were no queues, no order – just a massive crowd of frustrated passengers all trampling over each other trying to speak to one of the two poor souls at the help desk who were supposed to handle the situation. It was an utter mess. To make matters worse, many people missed their connecting flights because of the complete lack of organization.

Then came the lies – oh yes, we were promised by Air India staff that we would get our bags the same day. Well, guess what? Not only did that not happen, but no one at Air India could provide any useful information about when or where our bags were. We were told to "wait for the delivery" – but how are we supposed to wait when we don’t know when it will arrive, or even if it will arrive at all? It could be days, or it could be never. No updates, no tracking, no communication.

In desperation, we called Air India, the baggage delivery service, and even the airport multiple times. Each time we were given the same vague, unhelpful response: "Your bag will be delivered soon." Nothing more, nothing concrete. Meanwhile, we were stuck without any clothes or essentials in a country we don’t even live in – and Air India refused to give us any compensation. Why? Because we’re Indian citizens living abroad. Apparently, that means we’re not entitled to any help or support from the airline that lost our luggage.

It’s not just the inconvenience and chaos that is appalling – it’s the total lack of care, empathy, or professionalism from Air India. How can an airline get away with such abysmal service? No one should have to go through this. If you value your sanity, your belongings, and your dignity, avoid Air India at all costs. The whole experience was a nightmare and left us completely stranded and helpless. This is by far the worst airline experience I’ve ever had.

title: Air India: A Travel Experience Full of Disappointments
text:
I feel compelled to share our deeply disappointing experience with Air India, hoping it serves as a cautionary tale for others. My group of four recently traveled from Singapore to Chennai, and what should have been a smooth journey turned into a nightmare due to Air India’s poor service and lack of professionalism.

At Singapore Changi Airport

We arrived at Changi Airport at 5:00 PM for our scheduled 9:50 PM flight. Despite being early, we found no information about our flight on the display boards. After waiting for hours, we approached Air India staff multiple times for help, but all we received were vague responses asking us to “wait.” To our shock, the staff even resorted to checking the flight status on Google to give us updates!

When we were finally redirected to the check-in counters, there was complete chaos. We were sent back and forth between Zone 10 and Zone 9 with conflicting instructions. By the time we were allowed to check in our baggage, we were told boarding was closing in 20 minutes, creating unnecessary panic after waiting for hours.

Onboard Flight Experience

To make matters worse, the flight turned out to be Air India Express, not the Air India service we had booked and paid for.
	•	The flight lacked even basic amenities: no meals, no blankets, no pillows – nothing you’d expect for a 5-hour international flight.
	•	Even if we were willing to pay, the only items available for purchase were drinks and liquor.
	•	There was no onboard entertainment whatsoever, making the long journey even more tedious and uncomfortable.
	•	The seats were incredibly uncomfortable, adding to the overall discomfort during the flight.
	•	Since we had no time to grab food at the airport due to the last-minute rush, we were left hungry and restless throughout the flight.

At Chennai Airport – Terminal 2

Our ordeal didn’t end there. At Chennai Airport, we had a layover of over 6 hours in Terminal 2, and the experience was appalling:
	•	We were confined to an enclosed area with no access to duty-free shops or even a proper lounge.
	•	The seating was extremely hard and uncomfortable, making it impossible to rest.
	•	The area was dirty and poorly maintained, further adding to our discomfort.
	•	There was no Wi-Fi, which is shocking for an international airport.
	•	Food options were extremely limited, and we had to call for delivery to get something to eat, which we were forced to consume while being stared at by others in the crowded area.
	•	Communication was nearly impossible, as many of the airport staff didn’t speak English.

Our Expectations and Disappointment

We booked Air India expecting a certain level of service and reliability. Instead, we were forced onto an Air India Express flight, which is a budget airline, with none of the services we paid for. The lack of communication, mismanagement at check-in, absence of basic in-flight amenities, and the terrible layover conditions at Chennai Airport all point to a complete disregard for passenger comfort and satisfaction.

Final Thoughts

This was our first and last experience with Air India. For an airline that claims to represent India’s national pride, this was an embarrassing display of inefficiency and poor service. I cannot recommend Air India to anyone and strongly urge the airline to take immediate steps to improve its services.

If you value your time, money, and peace of mind, stay away from Air India.

text:

I was on flight AI 121 from New Delhi (DEL) to Frankfurt (FRA) on 06-03-2022, which was delayed by 5 hours and 15 minutes. This caused immense disruption to my travel plans, including additional expenses for pre-booked train and taxi tickets, and considerable stress while traveling with my 1-year-old child.

Despite repeated follow-ups and providing the necessary documentation (including the delay certificate issued by Air India), my rightful claim for compensation under EU regulations was rejected. The airline failed to provide any valid explanation or take accountability for the inconvenience caused. Their customer service was unhelpful and dismissive, further compounding the frustration.

Under EU Regulation 261/2004, passengers on delayed flights are entitled to compensation, and Air India’s refusal to adhere to these laws reflects poorly on their commitment to passenger rights.

I expected better from a national carrier and am disheartened by their lack of transparency and empathy. I would strongly urge other travelers to consider alternative airlines that value customer satisfaction and abide by international laws.

title: British Airways watch out, Air India’s new long haul business class has arrived
text:
I have to admit I was initially apprehensive when we booked our flights with Air India. 

Our travel agent was very honest and advised us of the historical problems especially with customer care. But the financial saving compared to British Airways (our usual airline) combined with hope that the new ownership would mean improvements were enticing enough for us to give Air India a go. 

Reading some other reviews, I was fully expecting a whole host of issues from broken seats to delays and lost baggage but I couldn’t have been more wrong. 

British Airways, you need to seriously up your business class game on Air India routes because currently, the BA offering is barely mediocre and very much over priced in comparison to Air India and you just can’t compete any longer! Air India’s new business class experience is more comparable to BA’s first class offering. 

Air India’s fully (flat) reclining seats are very comfortable and spacious with enough room in your very private pod for a lot of belongings in cupboards and drawers. The cabin crew make your bed for you and give you pyjamas. The touch screens are easy to use and we didn’t have any issues with them being slow or not working, The cabins were clean and kept clean (including the toilets) throughout the flight. 

The food was superb, A very good choice of Indian and Western options for vegetarians, meat eaters and pescatarians. It was high quality, presented beautifully, and was very tasty.

The cabin crew were consistently very attentive, kind and we didn’t have to do anything for ourselves. If we wanted anything we just had to ask. With BA  we often feel the cabin crew act like strict finger wagging school teachers there to police the aircraft rather than give passengers a positive experience. With Air India, we felt properly looked after and genuinely cared about (thoroughly spoilt in fact)  from start to finish. The business class service with Air India is akin to the business class experience we’ve had in the past with other very well respected airlines such as Cathay Pacific.

We had 2 long haul business class flights and 3 internal flights with Air India during our 16 day trip (Nov 2024) and every flight was bang on time and our checked in cases arrived in the baggage hall quickly and safely every time. 

If feasible, we’ll now be looking at Air India for all our future trips, even if it means having a short stop over in an Indian city en route. I can’t praise them enough. 

Well done Air India, what an achievement

We have abstained from Air India flights for a long while due to the awful experiences with the carrier. However, we decided to try again after the new management took over. Knowing the new owner's reputation, we hoped to have at least decent improvements in every aspect of the flight.

Of course, there are improvements in communication, cabin crew attitudes, and inflight food areas.

 However, major disappointments were when the check-in crew failed to keep our prebooked seats (both ways) and split the three seniors into different rows. They have no explanation or the right attitude to accommodate our prearranged seat.

The plane was the 777-300ER, the workhorse in their fleet. The flight was smooth and uneventful. The business cabin was clean, spacious, and outfitted with lay-flat seats. The toilets were cleaned frequently. Thanks to the courteous and service-minded cabin crew.

However,  a few video screens and seat adjustments were malfunctioned. We heard that a few seats were completely 'disabled'

Will we fly again on Air India? Yes: I hope the changes we see will be carried forward under the current management.

Furthermore, the food served was the same for all three meals, which was monotonous and unappetizing.

title: Better than anticipated, worth a try
text:
Our travel agent put us on this international flight from Dulles to New Delhi. I read some of the reviews only after getting the reservation and was filled with dread. So many negative reviews! But the tickets could not be changed.  So I was very pleasantly surprised with our flight. The only real negative thing to write is that the entertainment system, Vista, went out about mid-flight. Since this has happened to us before on other flights, we were prepared with e-reader and tablets. Even at its best, apparently Vista is not made for Windows computers and is restricted to certain browsers. My favorite browser was not one of them, unfortunately.

Okay, the negative part is out of the way. Air India stayed in step with us before, during and after the flight. Pre-flight I received regular messages about baggage weight limits, luggage content limits, check-in online (and its limits), Vista and what tags my checked-in luggage received. It was easy to pick out our seats, choose meals and establish our loyalty club ID. Leaving our bags at the counter took 3 minutes or less and the agent was very courteous.
Departure was close to on-time (I did not check precisely). The plane was clean and modern in appearance. As I mentioned, the entertainment system left us hanging about half-way through the 14 hour flight. Food was Indian fare; we liked it since we had not had any for the past 2 months in America. I don't think it could pass as major cuisine in a restaurant, but not bad for airline food. The bathrooms were typical, about average in cleanliness for a plane. They were adequately stocked with soap, toilet paper and paper towels. It does not seem that economy class will ever see very clean bathrooms again. I can say that the floor was clean and not sticky, so it was tolerable. The staff was generally friendly and usually smiling. In fact, the passengers themselves were on good behaviour despite the entertainment system outage. Announcements were made in English and Hindi about flight turbulence and other concerns when needed, but the PA system was difficult to understand.
Arrival was on time. After the flight, we got our bags within 10 minutes of getting out of customs (Delhi immigration is quicker than most US airports in my experience), which is about average in my experience for an international flight. A day later I received an email asking for an evaluation, to which I responded.

title: STAY AWAY - especially for domestic India travel - unless you like last minute changes at your expense
text:
Bottom line: Air India seems to change flights and keep our money. 

We purchased business class tickets for our domestic flights in India. In the end, they changed our tickets each time within weeks of the flight. 

- the first time, we paid more to avoid the 6am flight...then about 10-wks before the flight, Air India canx our flight and moved us to the 6am flight. When we asked for the fare difference to be refunded (because we paid more to AVOID the 6am flight), they said the ticket price was now the same cost as our ticket, so no refund was due
- the second flight was the only flight (the whole week) with a domestic business class section. All other flights were economy only. It was a 9:40pm - 11:40pm flight (not optimal, but we picked it because we needed the luggage allowance and leg room). Just over a month before the flight, we got a notice that they changed planes to an economy only configuration. Our travel agency has been trying to get the refund of the fare difference (it looks like they are trying to triple the price of the economy ticket value and refund us far less than we should receive) and get our seat assignment worked out, since we no longer have our business class seats. We can't get an official response. We were also just told we no longer have confirmed tickets since we haven't accepted their modification.  WHAT??? All we asked for was for them to confirm the refund due to us before we accepted the change, and they have never responded. They have had $680 for more than 6-months from us. The highest economy seats are worth $160 (total) and are still available, today. So here we sit, without a refund (which won't be processed until after we complete the flight in 3 weeks), and they won't confirm we still have tickets/seats until we accept their modification, which we won't accept until they confirm the refunded cost.

It's a great scheme. Get us to pay more each time, then change the deal just before our trip (knowing we can't do anything about it because all our other plans are locked in), then find a reason the refund isn't due (or is far less than it should be). 

We chose them because we trusted a Star Alliance brand. In both cases, we our travel plans were changed drastically (and for the worse) in the 11th hour at our expense. STAY AWAY, is our advice!!!

I contact Air India via email following my flight regarding the crew taking their rest breaks in the Business Class cabin, astonishingly I was informed that “crew are permitted to rest in vacant seats”.

Our experience was without doubt the worst treatment my partner and I have ever received from an airline. We have travelled extensively over many years.

Because of the late exit from Heathrow we had about 30 minutes to get to the departure gate. Even though we all arrived promptly we were told the gate had closed and we could not get on the flight. When the food arrived there was nothing I could eat as all the food was mixed in tubs!! I had noticed in a cafe  10 meters from where all this was happening there was food I could eat. Cost £2.50. When I enquired if they could buy this for me they were unbelievably rude and unconcerned. I don't believe we were asking for much from an airline which had failed to get us on to a connecting flight.

We later found out the connecting flight had actually been delayed to take on board our luggage and we could have indeed caught this plane. What a shambles! Air India consequently owe us compensation which under UK law should be paid in 7 days. 40 days later we are still awaiting payment and are unable to make direct contact with Air India.

Shame on you Air India. You are a total disgrace!

title: We were kept inside a 50°C hot cabin with a broken AC
text:
Let me present you with the wonderful 'New Air India Experience.

We boarded the 15-year-old Airbus A321, VT-PPW, on July 16th, 2024, around 1:30 p.m. for a scheduled departure at 2:15 p.m. The plane pushed back on time and started its engines. At that time, the outside temperature was 40°C, and it was around 35°C inside the plane.

Once the engines started, the plane moved just a couple of meters away from its original parking position but did not taxi to the runway. It soon became obvious to everyone that there was an issue with the air conditioning, as the cabin temperature continued to rise.

After 15 minutes without moving, the captain turned off the engines and informed us that the plane would be towed back to the gate to be inspected by Air India engineers. 

But instead of towing the plane back to the nearby parking position and letting passengers disembark into the terminal, the plane was towed for over 40 minutes across Delhi Airport to a remote parking area. Meanwhile, the cabin temperature rose to 50°C. There were elderly people and children on board, and passengers started to feel unwell.

Once we reached the remote parking position, passengers began shouting and arguing with Air India staff (onboard and ground), demanding to leave the dangerously hot plane, which by then had turned into a 50°C oven. We were finally allowed to disembark after more shouting and struggling, but this only happened after another hour in the unbearable heat, as Air India forced us to remain on board. Once we went through security again, we re-boarded the exact same plane, which had been repaired, and eventually reached Amritsar with a delay of about five hours. Fortunately the plane was just half empty, i would not imagine how the situation would have escalated if it would have been full.

My luggage did not arrive at Amritsar Airport. After filing a report, Air India staff informed me that it would arrive on the following flight a few hours later and be delivered to my hotel the next morning. I had to give them my WhatsApp number, and they provided me with their contact so that we could stay in touch. However, no one ever contacted me. My hotel called them 10 times, but no one answered. Since my luggage never reached the hotel, I went to the airport, and, to my great surprise, my luggage still there and no one was caring about the situation. After I started shouting and complaining to the staff, it was delivered to me within 15 minutes.

I have traveled a lot, but I have never ever seen such an unprofessional airline as Air India. The Air India cabin and ground staff were completely overwhelmed by the situation. Keeping passengers on board for so long, without air conditioning, in 50°C heat, in a country like India where people die every day from heatstroke, is incredibly irresponsible and unsafe.

Furthermore, I also want to mention that I have never seen a cabin in such a desperate state as the one on this Air India A321. The seats were broken and many of them wouldn't even recline, the seat fabric was torn apart, and everything was filthy.

If Air India truly wants to transform from a low-quality airline (which it still is today) into the 'New Pride of India', there is a very, very long way to go. The horrible reputation built over decades cannot simply be washed away with rebranding and new uniforms for the cabin crew.

As a foreigner visiting India, I was appalled by the service and quality of this airline, and I do not recommend it for your travel

What an extreme disappointment and frustration with the recent flight my family and I took from London to Delhi. The experience was nothing short of a nightmare. Considering the high cost of the tickets, the standards we encountered were appalling and unacceptable.
The Seats: The condition of the seats was beyond belief. It felt as if we were sitting on broken wooden panels, barely disguised with a thin, torn piece of cloth. Instead, we were provided with two additional seat covers—despite there being three of us traveling. In-Flight Entertainment: The in-flight entertainment was another disaster. None of the three screens in our row functioned properly. The plastic frames were broken, charger points were missing (leaving only holes where they should have been), and one screen was completely absent. We reported this issue, and the Flight Manager attempted to help by moving us to crew seats. However, the situation was no better there. The screens were still non-functional, and to make matters worse, one of the tray tables was missing, forcing us to eat our meals on our laps. When we requested an additional seat cover for our 11-year-old daughter, the request was flatly refused. We decided to move to our original seats to be able to eat our meals properly.
The Crew’s Response: The most disheartening part of this experience was the response we received from one of the air hostesses. When we complained about our broken seats, she simply said, "Please don’t worry, it is the last month. From September, Air India will have new planes with much better conditions!" While I appreciate that improvements are on the horizon, this does nothing to address the suffering we endured on this particular flight in August. We paid a premium price for a service that was far below acceptable standards. This plane should never have been allowed to fly with passengers on board, given its condition.

title: A new Air India under Tata?
text:
I believe I might be one of the first people to give a five-star rating to an airline after missing a connecting flight due to a delay. Recently, I traveled from Delhi to Paris on AI 143 in business class, and I have to say I was pleasantly surprised by the top-quality service I received from the moment I boarded.

The cabin crew went above and beyond to provide exceptional service. I was also amazed by the quality of the food served on the flight. Not only did it look fantastic, but it tasted even better than what you’d find in some gourmet restaurants. I believe these improvements are a result of Air India's new ownership under Tata.

While the aircraft itself was a bit old, the cabin crew informed me that new planes are on the way. They were genuinely excited about working under the new ownership and seemed optimistic about Air India's future.

Unfortunately, our departure from Delhi was delayed by approximately two hours, leading to a late arrival in Paris and causing me to miss my connecting Air France flight. Although Air France rebooked me for the next morning, they couldn’t offer additional assistance since the delay was caused by Air India. However, the staff at the Air India counter at the airport were incredibly helpful. One lady in particular assured me that she would take care of everything, and she did just that. She arranged hotel accommodation for the night, provided food vouchers for dinner and breakfast, and organized shuttle service to and from the hotel.

These experiences are a refreshing departure from what many have come to expect from the old Air India. Based on my experience, I’m happy to say that Air India is in good hands and I look forward to seeing them become a globally recognized airline, providing an excellent flying experience in the future.

title: Avoid this airline if you can.
text:
We had to book a last minute flight and chose Air India due to lower fares and a relatively short stop-over in Delhi. We spent €2,500 for two tickets scheduled to depart in a few days (due to a family emergency).

Well, you get what you pay for. In-flight entertainment did not work for anyone on BOTH flights, meaning we were in an airplane for 20+ hours combined with none of the screens working. Woeful!

The chairs and tray tables felt extremely old and worn down, and my coxic bone is still sore from how hard the chairs felt.

The food, yikes, so bad. All the meals tasted like they had been stuck in a busted freezer for years before being quickly reheated for our consumption. Each piece of bread that came with the meals turned my mouth into a desert, and the desserts weren't any better either.

The less I say about the lavatories on the plane, the better. Think of something disgusting, multiply that by 100, and you'll come close to the level of cleanliness seen in these toilets. I've seen portable toilets on music festivals in better states than these things.

Our stop over in Delhi sucked too. To get through international transfers was such a chore, I could write a book about that experience. Long story short: all staff members are stressed and in a constant state of chaos, nobody knows what's going on or what to do, and everything took a million times longer than it should have. 

So yeah, not good. If you have no choice and you have a limited budget, you will at least arrive safe and with your baggage intact, but that's the only good thing I can say. Hence why I am giving 2 stars instead of 1. 

In any other scenario, avoid at all cost.

title: A Nightmare in the Skies: Air India Flight AI186
text:
Traveling should be a comfortable and stress-free experience, especially when flying business class and having paid a premium for what is expected to be exceptional service. Unfortunately, our experience with Air India flight AI186 shattered any expectations we had for a decent flight, let alone a pleasurable one. 

My elderly parents, with my father recently recovering from a stroke and requiring significant assistance, embarked on this journey, and what ensued was nothing short of a nightmare. From start to finish, Air India demonstrated a blatant disregard for customer care, particularly for those in need of special assistance. 

At the airport, despite having pre-booked assistance, we were met with complete indifference. There was no one available to help my parents through the check-in process, and they had to walk to the boarding gate. The very essence of customer service was non-existent, as though assisting elderly passengers was an inconvenience to their day.

The situation only worsened upon landing at Delhi International Airport. My parents were once again left to navigate the vast and bustling airport without any guidance or support. The promised wheelchair assistance was nowhere to be found, and attempts to seek help from Air India staff were met with cold shoulders and dismissive attitudes. It was appalling to witness my father, still recovering from a stroke, struggle to walk through the airport, and my mother, equally elderly, try to manage their belongings without any aid. 

What is the point of paying for a business class ticket if the service is this abysmal? The cost was supposed to ensure a certain standard of care and comfort, but Air India failed spectacularly on all fronts. Their inability to provide even the most basic assistance highlights a systemic problem within their operations, one that shows a complete lack of consideration for passengers' needs.

This experience has been a revelation in the worst possible way. Not only did Air India fail to deliver on their promises, but they also managed to create an incredibly stressful and exhausting ordeal for my parents. The level of negligence and unprofessionalism displayed is unacceptable and inexcusable. It is clear that Air India does not value its customers, especially those who are vulnerable and in need of extra care.

I will never book a ticket with Air India again, and I strongly advise anyone, particularly those traveling with elderly family members or individuals who need assistance, to avoid this airline at all costs. The high price of a business class ticket does not equate to high-quality service with Air India. Instead, it seems to fund their gross incompetence and lack of customer care.

In conclusion, our experience with Air India flight AI186 was a disastrous one, marred by poor service, lack of assistance, and a blatant disregard for customer well-being. Save yourself the distress and choose an airline that values and respects its passengers. Air India, unfortunately, is not that airline.

title: Poor product and service, through and through!
text:
It was the WORST travel experience I have ever had with any Airline. I traveled from Hyderabad, India, to Toronto via Delhi with my seven-year-old daughter; it was her first ultra-long-haul flight(Delhi to Toronto), so I paid in advance for seats with extra legroom and in a row with just two seats. 

My challenges started right from the booking time itself

Chapter 1—Poor booking experience: somehow, after the booking was processed, the system incorrectly recorded our passport numbers and DOBs. It took me hours to contact customer care, but I eventually corrected it.

Chapter 2 - Extremely poor web-check-in: so the system didn't allow me to web check in, and I noticed that my daughter's seat number had changed to a middle seat in a random row that was several rows ahead of my paid(row 42) and booked seat(row 18). At the airport, I discovered they separated me and my daughter for a ~15-hour flight because my daughter couldn't be seated at an emergency exit row, and they just changed her seat without even an intimation. While booking and paying for those seats, the system happily accepted the payment but later had the epiphany that a minor can't occupy emergency row seats.

Chapter 3 - Airport check-in: as I tried reasoning with the airport staff that I have paid for these extra-legroom seats and your system accepted the payment, their initial response was, "NOT MY PROBLEM" You'll get different seats, take it or leave it. And I can contact customer care later for a refund. When I didn't budge, saying I had already paid and I wanted those seats, one of their smarter ones said she found the same seats with the same two-seat-only layout in a different row, and she was changing my seats, and I wouldn't get any refund. I was happy, and I took those and went ahead to board.

Chapter 4 - First leg of the journey aircraft: when I boarded the Hyd-Del leg, it was decades old and absolutely not maintained Boeing-777. Broken screens, stained seats, smelly cabin, the list doesn't end. Literally, while taxing to the runway, the aircraft creaked like an old ST bus, making me worry about the fitness of the aircraft to fly(thankfully, it landed in Delhi uneventfully). This aircraft also flew internationally. Honestly, I felt ashamed as an Indian that this is what we are projecting to the world as our quality.

Chapter 5 - The lie of same extra-leg room: Before landing in Delhi, I checked the newly allocated row (no.43) in the Hyd-Del plane(both my flights were in B777 with the same seat configurations), which didn't have extra-leg room but was in that two seat only config. After landing in Delhi, I reached out to Air India support staff once again before the immigration counter; they asked me to go out of the airport with a sleepy seven-year-old at midnight, discuss with their superior, and find a solution. Well, no solution, and I boarded the flight after getting rude responses. After boarding my next flight, I found out that the seats(row 43) allocated to me were snatched from someone traveling with his senior citizen mother and had booked and paid for those seats in October 2023 (we traveled in April 2024). They were pushed to some random middle seats in a different row, and all this happened without their consent. 

Chapter 6—Poor staff behavior: Thankfully, the next aircraft from Del to Toronot was much better from the inside and the outside. It was still dirty, yes, but slightly more maintained. It was no where close to other flag carriers, but better than my Hyd-Del one. Typically, if you need something while traveling with any other airline, you would press a button, and a crew member will come to help out. Here, the button just made a sound and lit a small bulb above my head, and nothing else happened. Even for water, I had to walk up to the galley and ask. Wanted veg food - response: we are out of veg, so take chicken or stay hungry. Want one more 30 ml drink? - response: Air India doesn't serve more than one at a time, so they will serve the next one after four hours. Pls, wait in your seat (I am still waiting). Since when is this the rule? Response: even since I've worked with Air India. Before landing, the head of the flight crew reached out to me, asking what had happened about the drink, sir. I told him what was told me by the flight crew, and he was surprised that they didn't serve because I was well in my rights to ask for one more drink. Later, ever since I've worked with Air India's response, I got to know she was just two months old and hired at Air India(ROFL). 

Chapter 7—The refund: I contacted customer care for a refund for the fraud with the seat allocation, and they asked me to register a complaint on their website. It's been more than a month and over 10 email exchanges, and I'm still waiting for them to process my refund. 

Honestly, I have never seen any airline mistreat their customers so much with such ill-maintained aircraft and rude staff. I was hopeful the airline would be around after the Tata takeover, but it still seems like a distant dream.

title: Bad to worse under the Tata's
text:
The Airline was on a downhill spiral since almost 16 years if not more. When the Tata's took over people had high hope for its recovery. However even after 28 months things are as bad if not worse.  I avoid flying this airline and rarely do unless I have no better options. 

It's a big let down for a Tata company. I do not know if there is any other business in this group that is anywhere even close to as bad as Air India is now.

title: Good care by Air India after flight was cancelled
text:
I had an unfortunate incident with Air India. We (four persons of family) were to fly from Tirupati to Delhi by AI-541 on Sunday, 14 April 2024 (PNR UUKALB). We reported at the airport on time around 12:30 PM and got the boarding passes. The Delhi-Hyderabad-Tirupati flight (which was to take us to Delhi as AI-541) arrived at Tirupati before time. But while landing at Tirupati airport, it got hit by a bird and needed repaires. Air India staff at Tirupati airport kept on announcing delay by half an hour every half an hour and after 4 PM there was no announcement though water and snacks were provided. Around 6 pm, we were told that the flight has been cancelled and we were required to get a different flight. Options were the same flight next day from Tirupati (which already had only limited seats available) or 6 am flight from Chennai or any other flight from Chennai to Delhi next day i.e. Monday 15 April. Since we were 04 persons, we could get the 20:40 PM flight from Chennai to Delhi (AI 538) for which Air India told us that they would take us to Chennai and will make our stay arrangements in Chennai. So around 20:30 PM on Sunday, they provided a bus, which was quite comfortable, and could accommodate 23 persons. We reached Chennai Airport at around 00:30 am on 15 April. After dropping those who were to catch the 06:00 am flight at the airport, they arranged for our stay in a Hotel in Chennai. The Hotel Feathers - a radha group of hotels, had picked us up in their vehicle and we reached the hotel at around 01:30 am. The Feathers Hotel was located at around half an hour drive away from airport and it was a decent (perhaps 4* if not a 5* hotel). The hotel provided Breakfast, Lunch and free pick and drop facility. After the whole day fatigue, it was quite relaxing in the hotel.
Except for incomplete announcements at Tirupati Airport (which I can understand as they had sent all the details of repair work to DGCA and had sought their permission to fly the aircraft and DGCA was not responding), other arrangements (snacks, water, transport to Chennai, hotel arrangements in Chennai, pick and drop to and from hotel were handled excellently by the Manager and his staff at Tirupati Airport and at Chennai Airport.
Our thanks to Air India and its staff for the courtesies shown by them.
Pradeep Kumar

Air India was totally unprofessional, no support, so many of us missed our connections and they did not even prepare ahead though they knew more than 24 hrs ahead that this flight was delayed  from SFO.

The only flight I got to MAA was the next day April 19th at 7am via Mumbai, another 5 hour flight for what is usually 1 hour!

They put us up in a cheap 3-star hotel overnight. Imagine, I was forced into a 14.5 hours "layover" just to get from BLR to MAA. 
I will never fly Air India.
I was rooting for AI.
The point is - it's not about when things are good or that sh*t happens in life, it is the professional and considerate treatment given to a paying customer when said sh*t happens that matters.

title: WORST EVER
text:
Subject: Worst Experience with Air India - Unacceptable Treatment and Incompetence

Dear Air India,

I am writing this email to express my utmost dissatisfaction and disgust with the treatment my group and I received from Air India during our recent travel experience. Our flight, scheduled to depart from Incheon on April 16th, with a layover in Delhi before reaching Dubai, was cancelled due to a natural disaster in Dubai. While we understand that the cancellation was unavoidable given the circumstances, Air India's handling of the situation was absolutely unacceptable and demonstrated a severe lack of competence and concern for your passengers.

During our grueling 8-hour wait at the airport, we were left without any proper accommodation to rest or sleep. Our group of over 10 people was forced to endure the long hours without any food or a place to even lie down. To make matters worse, when we inquired about the situation, your staff was unable to provide us with any clear explanations and instead chose to ignore us and attend to other matters. This complete disregard for your passengers' well-being is appalling and inexcusable.

Moreover, two members of our group suffer from rare diseases and had all their medication packed in their checked luggage. Despite our desperate attempts to retrieve their bags, we were told that it was not possible due to regulations. While we understand the need for such rules, what followed next was an absolute nightmare. Upon arriving in Oman, we discovered that our luggage had not been sent by Air India at all. This is utterly unacceptable and demonstrates a severe lack of responsibility and care on your part.

The experience we had with Air India was hands down the worst travel experience of our lives. We cannot fathom how an airline can treat its passengers with such disregard and incompetence. Rest assured, we will never fly with Air India again, and we will make sure to share our horrendous experience with everyone we know. If legal action were an option, we would not hesitate to pursue it, given the severity of the situation.

Your airline's conduct was the epitome of poor service and unprofessionalism. We demand a full explanation and compensation for the emotional, physical, and financial distress you have caused us. This experience has left us utterly disgusted and disappointed, and we expect Air India to take full responsibility for their actions.

title: The Worst Airline in 2024: Air-India, its Staff and Management
text:
We purchased two premium economy class tickets on Air India Flights 626 and 119 from Lucknow-Mumbai to New York (JFK). Flight 626 (Lucknow to Mumbai) on March 29 and Flight 119 (from Mumbai to JFK, NY) on March 30. When we checked-in at Lucknow airport, boarding passes for both flights were printed. While walking away from the counter, I realized that on Mumbai to New York, about 16-hour flight, we were assigned seats in the economy class instead of Premium class, though I had paid for the premium class which is about 3-times the cost of economy class ticket. Next two hours I argued with Air India staff (Air India Duty Manager and Head of staff at Lucknow airport) without any success; they refused to honor our premium tickets. While in the Air-India office, Air-India duty manager (March 29 at 1 pm) asked me to go away and seek help from their call center! I handed over them my phone and asked him to connect to the call center. Somebody at the call center picked up my call after 40 minutes while I was in their office. Call center person was also puzzled that I was in the Air India office and the duty manager was asking me to seek help from the call center. Call center staff refused to help and asked airport staff to resolve it. After reaching Mumbai, I went to Air-India office at Mumbai airport and spent 90 minutes arguing with them. In the end I ended up sitting in a cramped economy seat for 16 hours. It appeared that there were not enough passengers for the big aircraft, therefore Air India down-graded plane on that route on March 30. Down-graded smaller plane was without premium class seats; therefore, Air India dumped us in the economy class. Any other airline would have upgraded our seats in this situation, but Air India staff asked us to buy new full prize business class tickets for the upgrade (that was beyond our budget). 

The downgraded plane came to the gate around 12:30 AM (March 30) for a scheduled take off at 1:45 AM. But soon engineering crews were all over the plane and opened the side panels and found major mechanical defect, and did not clear aircraft to fly. After 3 hours of repair, boarding started at 4:45 AM. As soon as we walked into the cabin, we realized that it was a very old plane with non-functional analog TV screens hanging from the ceiling. It was clear that any maintenance or upgrade was not done in the cabin since this plane was put in service about 20-years ago.

Cushions on seats were compacted over years and it seems that we were sitting on wooden chairs without any cushion. Cushions on the seats were slipping off exposing metal frame underneath (see picture). Wires and cable towards the window side of the seats were fully exposed and loose (see picture). Plastic cover over the seat frame were duct-taped (see picture). All tray-tables (on the back of the seat) were broken (see picture); it could not stay straight and stable. 
Entertainment system did not work at all. Screen and remote were not functional (see picture). I checked with other passengers, and everybody complained that it did not work.

During the 16-hour flight, it appeared that the washroom was not cleaned or serviced at all.

You will be very lucky if you get any refund (difference between premium and economy class). If you are persistent and follow through, somehow, they block your email address and your message (or argument) will bounce back undelivered after successfully sending emails to care@airindia.com. When they were unable to deal with my arguments, they blocked me. After a long-convoluted process and providing them with a copy of our passport, e-ticket, boarding pass, case Id and complete details of our bank account, Air India offered to issue a credit voucher that will be valid for one year. Who wants to fly with Air India again after this experience?
I came across several complaints where premium and business class passengers were downgraded to economy class and were not given any logical reason and compensation. It is not only very poorly maintained old tattered aircraft but also Air-India ground staff and management are incompetent and are not customer friendly at all. In summary Air-India is the worst airline that I came across after flying on international routes for 36 years.

title: TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE! A RATING OF 0 WOULD BE MORE APPROPRIATE!
text:
As a seasoned traveler, my recent flight with Air India left much to be desired, prompting me to share my experience for the benefit of fellow passengers. Despite reaching out to their Customer Success Team repeatedly over the past seven months, the response has been disappointingly inadequate, leaving me with no choice but to voice my concerns publicly.

From the outset, the flight was marred by delays, lack of communication, and a general disregard for passenger comfort. The compensation offered—a mere 30 euros per person—was not only insulting but laughable given the magnitude of inconvenience endured during the flight delay. 

Furthermore, the condition of the aircraft was subpar, with broken entertainment systems rendering videos unwatchable for the duration of the over eight-hour flight. Coupled with inadequate cleanliness, substandard food quality, and uncomfortably cramped seating, the overall experience was far from satisfactory.

Despite repeated attempts to seek clarification regarding their internal investigations and grounds for denying compensation, responses from Air India's Customer Success Team were evasive and unsatisfactory. This lack of transparency only added to the frustration of an already unpleasant journey.

In conclusion, my experience with Air India was marred by a lack of accountability, poor customer service, and glaring quality issues. I hope this review serves as a cautionary tale for fellow travelers considering Air India for their future journeys.

Transit was in Delhi indira gandhi international airport. It was a smooth journey from frankfurt to Delhi. My luggage was according to the luggage allowance. But in delhi after checking I put some of my personal item  in hand luggage and I had to change my clothes because it's 24° celsius temperature in delhi and I was wearing layers of clothes because in frankfurt as the temperature was celsius 6-8° c. So after changing I had put my jacket and sweater in the hand luggage of course. Was I going to carry all in hand? Of course NO. So before bearding the lady stopped because she found some extra kilos. But I had explained her I was wearing puffy jackets and sweaters before and I've just changed. She said that's your personal item there is nothing we can do. I mean seriously? And they were not charging everyone. Some were boarding even after finding out extra kilos. There was the guy who was called to take payment. He was telling the lady let her go, another officer also wasn’t charging on the other line. So he said as he's not charging don't charge her. She said, "no. She has to pay. That's not how airlines work." If it's not how airlines work then how come an officer of the same airline was not charging? It's not about payment but if I had got sick wearing the jackets in this temperature of delhi was she gonna take the liability or the airlines? They should make things clear about it. The same airline from frankfurt to delhi didn’t have any problem but in delhi it was just harassment. They should be more professional about their rules. If there are rules then it should be followed in everywhere and for everyone. Not for anyone particular or according to the officer's choice. I've always used Qatar airlines and Turkish Airlines for this route but never had to experience such scene in transit. So if you're travelling from frankfurt with air india (not an  indian) and don't want to be embarrassed in your journey then avoid this airlines. And lastly thank you for this amazing experience Air India. First time but NEVER AGAIN.

text:
I recently experienced a 2-hour flight delay with Air India from London to Udaipur, resulting in a missed connecting flight to Udaipur, next flight was 24hrs later. This delay had a significant impact on my travel plans, causing me to miss an important day of a wedding ceremony.

After the inconvenience and disappointment of the delay, I reached out to Air India's customer service to address the situation. While they offered a compensation of £520 as a goodwill gesture, I must express my disappointment with this outcome.

The offered amount does not adequately reflect the extent of the inconvenience, discomfort, and financial loss we experienced due to the delay. They provided 1-star hotel accommodation did not meet basic comfort standards, further adding to the frustration.

I understand that airlines have their policies, but I expected more understanding and consideration given the circumstances. I have tried to negotiate further, but Air India has stated that this is their final offer.

As a customer, I believe that a higher compensation amount would have been more appropriate, considering the impact on my travel plans and the missed event. It is disappointing to feel undervalued as a passenger, especially in a situation that was within the airline's control.

I hope this review serves as feedback for Air India to revaluate their compensation policies for such situations. As a frequent traveller, I expect better customer service and consideration for passengers facing such disruptions.

title: Air India’s staff repeatedly lied to us for months in advance about pet travel. No accountability, just a delayed flight
text: I arrived in Chicago a day early to go to the airport ahead of our flight and show Air India staff the dog kennel we had purchase after significant amount of online investigation, just as one final verification that it was of the size and built with the hardware that were compliant with airline policy. It was only then, standing in the air port, 7 months, hundreds if not thousands of dollars, and many hours of preparation later, that I was told that Air India does not fly pets from the US to India (our layover was in Delhi). Now at that point I struggled to do anything and everything in my power to assure the staff of the fact that our pets travel had indeed already been approved and that multiple email communications and phone calls with customer representatives verified this. Surely Air India could not believe that we would have bought a one way ticket to the other side of the world bringing our beloved pet without repeatedly checking the requirements and regulations, but regardless of what we had been told (we showed them our emails) they said there was no possibility our pet was flying with us. As alluded to by our one way ticket, we were not going on a short vacation, we were moving to Nepal, for at the very least one year, with no return flights booked. The only reason we were choosing to fly with Air India was that after research, we (prematurely) trusted them with our pet more than some of the other airlines which had daunting reviews about the welfare of passenger’s pets. However, had we known that Air India does not fly pets from the US on any direct flight to India (something every single customer service representative should have been aware of had they been properly trained) we would have found an alternative means of getting our pet to Nepal. However, with less than 24 hours notice that our pet was in fact not able to travel, we had no recourse but to leave them in the US (with family, thank God), and go without them, a decision that was emotionally devastating, on top of causing us a significant amount of wasted money on preparation. We were given no explanation, redress, recourse or compensation from Air India. I originally submitted this message directly to Air Indias complaint department a month ago, but upon receiving nothing more ameliorating than a “we regret the inconvenience” email, I have decided to publicly review this company, and I wish to say that I do not leave negative public reviews as I always prefer to allow management of businesses an opportunity to fix there mistakes after consultation in private, but this egregious error on behalf of Air India has not been rectified and I feel the pinki should be aware of the ramifications of flying your loved ones, human or animal, with a company such as this. For the record: The AI director at Chicago O’Hare was kind and attempted to work with Turkish Airlines to do a ticket exchange, but after hours of negotiating the viability of that plan, and much waiting while they were behind the ticket counters in their offices (it felt like being held up by a used car salesman), we were finally given an offer of “potentially” being able to fly with our dog the following day, abandoning our confirmed reservation with Air India in lieu of a flight on Turkish for the small price of $5300. Perhaps if we in fact possessed that much liquid cash we would have allowed ourselves to be robbed in this manner, with the hopes of traveling with our pet, but it wasn’t even a possibility for us. So we would be moving without our beloved pet. To add insult to injury, our flight was delayed by 12 hours, and our connecting flight (also by Air India) by an additional 2 hours. title: Poor service, especially for long-haul flights
text:
I have travelled on Air India for many years right since my childhood while travelling between England and India - I recently travelled on 2nd February from London Heathrow to Kolkata via Mumbai and on 24th February 2024 from Kolkata back to Heathrow via Mumbai. However, I can say that the on board service, especially for long-haul international flights was quite poor (I usually fly through Economy) and really needs major improvements in future. 

The reasons for that are that they no longer provide in-flight monitor maps for longer fights (between 6-10 hours or more) - which is rather appalling for long distance flights as everyone has the right to know where exactly the plane is flying (really feels like a downgrade as there were usually in-flight maps years ago), the refreshment snacks could do with more choices (years ago they used to give peanuts which I liked but they now give some sort of corn snacks which wasn't too bad but more choices would be nice), the non-veg meals aren't always available and tend to run out more than the vegetarian meals (a few more meal choices would also be nicer for that), the film choices for films outside Hindi films was somewhat limited (I noticed when travelling towards Mumbai from Heathrow there were films like Oppenheimer & one of the recent Mission Impossible films but on my return journey back to Heathrow, they were no longer available), when the TV screens become faulty or crash (which seems more common now) the on-board crew don't seem to know how to fix them (whenever I've asked for the screens to be fixed or rebooted, the problem usually stays the same), and cleanliness in some areas needs some work. 

Another issue I have with Air India is that while the domestic flights are a bit better, there don't always seem to be as much updates when flight delays happen - my flight from Mumbai to Kolkata had a 3-hour delay but it took some time for the crew to update the passengers about the progress - which was supposedly down to poor visibility in Kolkata (might as well have deboarded the passengers back to the airport until the flight was ready to depart) while my return domestic flight to Mumbai got delayed and there was no update from the pilots or crew members about the reasons for that delay nor did they apologise for it which almost resulted in my & my family missing our connecting flight back to Heathrow (thankfully that flight waited for us and a few other delayed passengers).

Anyway, some positives are that most flights are usually on time and long delays are rare - that being said I'm not a frequent flyer, some of the crew members are quite polite & friendly (although there have been a few who were rude), the meals can be quite tasty when cooked/prepared well (although it can be a bit spicy/bland sometimes), the drink selection is good and it does have quite an extensive flight coverage inside India. However, the on-board service needs major improvements if they expect to be  world-class airline in the future - the Tata takeover initially made me hopeful for that although it is still taking them time to fix the issues I've mentioned (although I've read they're planning to refurbish some of the older fleet later this year which I hope does happen). I remember flying on Emirates when I was much younger and the service on Emirates was far superior than Air India even on Economy - more food/meal choices, in-flight maps on most flights, better selection of films, TV screens could be fixed during the flight if they became faulty and better cleanliness (if anyone from Air India reads this - take note). 

Unless Air India steps up their game in future - for which I could do an updated review, I would happily return to flying through Emirates in the future (or even try other airlines like Qatar Airways) if I am travelling alone - I usually fly through Air India when with my family as they for some reason prefer that in spite of its major flaws.

title: Budget airlines - better choice than Star Alliance Air India - The worst in all categories!
text:
The airline is part of the Star Alliance but don't be fooled by this! It is not a airline that lives up to the normal standard of Star Alliance and in my personal opinion should be forced out of the Alliance. It is very poor quality in all aspects. I am sorry to say that even though I tested many airlines over the years this is probably the worst all categories. Even including low price budget airlines. Why you might wonder. Well. Hera are some examples why ... The plane was supposed to have inflight entertainment (as all airlines have) but the majority of the screens were not working. Might be a problem in one plane but as it was the same on both flights it is most probably a systematic problem. Please prepare to have your own entertainment with you. The food onboard was really bad (normally I like the kind of food served in India but this was really bad). Take something to eat with you if you are foolish enough to go by Air india... The plane was dirty and even though the space was fairly good I would warn you for the not so pleasant flight. Service was ok but the limits of all type of drinks was not good (I only drink nonalcoholic and still there was limits)...
Now to maybe the worst problem ... My travel was delayed by almost 5 hours and that was according to the staff on the ground due to technical problems at first and then after finding an alternative plane they needed another crew as the other had to many hours. Ok that can happen and as we then are to be compensated by EU law with 600 Euros it is somewhat ok even though it is not nice as they kept reschedule by 15 min and no food or drink was offered (this is of course in direct conflict with international and EU law that demands free drinks and food on all delays more than 4 hours. This might be a good reminder of making sure I documented all the delay and got it in writing from the ground crew, which I didn't as I trusted a Star Alliance member to fulfill its obligations without any excuses). Now you might understand that when i asked for the legal compensation of 600 Euros (not for a full refund even though the entertainment, food etc weren't up to standard) they suddenly changed the delay cause to bad weather and not technical issues! This is a loophole in the law (which of course is correct as the weather is not something they can control but as there were other planes departing and arriving and the fact that the staff told us the technical issues, the change of plane and crew it is simply a way to avoid compensating). 
I would say that even though the Air India cost was lower than alternatives and that we believed Star Alliance to keep a good quality among their members we are extremely unhappy with Air India. I would urge anyone to take a second to evaluate if you really should book with this airline! I wouldn’t! It can be quite a bad start to your journey, and it is simply not worth the save! I would suggest you look at any other airline even budget before you choose Air India. We trusted Star Alliance and the fact that Air India is part of TATA as I also trust to be a professional business with a leader that shown great success. But his airline is a total disaster I am sorry to say. 
If I was TATA I would quickly erase my logo from this as it is really bad for the company image!

title: PATHETIC EXPERIENCE ALWAYS HEARD BUT FINALLY EXPERIENCED
text: On the 14th of January 2024 I travelled from Sydney to Mumbai via Delhi with my wife and 11-year-old daughter with Air India Flight number AI 301. The flight was delayed from 10:15 am to 14:30We reached Delhi around 9pm IST, instead of 17:40. our initial connection from Delhi to Mumbai was at 21:20. We completed the immigration: process at Delhi Picked up our Luggage and tried to check with Air India counter for our connecting flight. There was no assistance at the counter, The agent said she don't know anything and i will have to wait for her supervisor to arrive. After 10 minutes a gentlemen arrived and I informed him the situation, he said I need to go out and go to level 2. We went to the second floor (again no assistance by Air India). At level 2 after searching for 2 Air India counters Finally a counter issued us a boarding pass for flight AI605 with boarding time  0:45 am. Tired with the long and delayed flights we still hope that things would be smooth, to our surprise the flight was delayed to 2:45 am.( Note: No AI staff available at the boarding gates to inform .) At 4 am they announced that the flight was cancelled. Finally, an AI duty Manager arrived and informed that we need to collect out luggage from the belt and move to the AI reservation after exiting the airport where they have all arrangements ready. I did inform him that i am an Australian citizen with no contacts in Delhi and have travelled with AI from Sydney with my wife and 11year old daughter. He mentioned everything will be taken care of (Video Evidence available) We picked up our Luggage and went to the Reservation counter and to our surprise there were around 1000 to 1200 people stranded with no help from Air India. The arrangement was a chaotic, It was a cold Delhi early morning with my wife and daughter out in 5 to 6 degrees suddenly after the 20-degree Sydney Summer. Finally, I got hold of Mr Vikram Vats I am not sure if I pronounce the last name properly but i can provide evidence as I have his ID picture. I showed him my Australian passports and Boarding passes for AI 301 informed him that i have arrived from Sydney and had a connection to Mumbai. To my surprise he said he can't provide you either an alternate flight nor an accommodation so please find your alternate mode or even hotel and then take refund from AI. I didn't speak a word as my priority was to make sure my wife and daughter was safe and well, in this cold weather of Delhi. First, I booked a hotel room online on my own , got a taxi reached the hotel. Then booked for 3 Tatkal Tickets for Rajdhani express for 16th Jan. My wife and daughter was not very happy with this as they had heard a lot of stories about thefts in Indian Trains, but i had no option. As my hotel room was close to the airport my wife woke me up around 3am when she heard the sound of aircrafts landing and taking off, She asked me to go to the airport and check for the last time if we can get any rescheduled flight to Mumbai. I reached the airport at around 4 am I enquired about the tickets and the agent said why are you coming after 2 days > It was so annoying as there was no apology but instead they showed it as my mistake, I just kept quiet and took my tickets and went off, (Note there was no follow up email from Air India to check my whereabouts in Delhi on the 15th Jan Since they had cancelled AI 605.) In my 15 years of travel history this was the first time I travelled by Air India thinking it was taken over by TATA, but I was wrong. The Mental stress through which we went was immense, It took almost a week for my daughter to overcome this stress. Our Vacation was already spoiled even before it started (Thanks to the AI Delhi staff situation handling)
