title: Not reassuring
text:
I booked a return flight with Air India from London to Bangkok via New Delhi.
The first impression I got as I boarded was that the plane was dirty. There was still litter from the previous passengers! I am however a very patient guy, so I thought perhaps they didn't have much time to clean and were pressured by tight schedules etc so It didn't bother me that much, after all my own seating area was clean...
As I sat down in my thinly cushioned steel frame - the seat (for a 9h flight to New Delhi) I couldn't help but notice a slight jiggle in my chair... The reason being it was NOT properly screwed to the floor. At this point I admit that I got slightly worried but said nothing nevertheless (if a plane will crash, screw or no screw, you're screwed). Before takeoff, in the row of seats next to me was a drunk indian man. He was already fighting with the hostess to exchange seats with someone unrelated to him for some reason. I silently prayed he wouldn't be seated next to me for 9h. Eventually he settled down somewhere.The flight itself went smoothly apart from a few turbulences where the plane shook like cardboard, but no problems other than a million children running around, crying babies and the smell of curry... Of course, don't expect your TV to work in the plane. Mine was seemingly broken, as well as the remote to use it. The arm-rest too.
Arriving at New Delhi Airport: Be prepared to show your passport and boarding pass around from the first step out of the plane. I must have had to show it a couple dozen times and wait in queues of people to pass security where one soldier would be S L O W L Y pushing your bags through the scanners one at a time (with what seemed like no concern about anything in the world) and 5 others literally doing nothing to help. Also be prepared for people to just walk in front of you in queues. Return flight was very much the same except I did get a screen which worked, but then found out the choice of films is of around 4... Also, I paid more than I did with other companies for the same destination, so I do NOT recommend.

best if you travelling with infant.

title: Did the job

title: Horrible service, bad food and smelly flight
text:
Flight was scheduled to start at 1:15 PM, so most passengers did not eat lunch. Flight started at 2:15 PM and lunch was served at 4:00 PM. By that time, most passengers were really frustrated. The first thing you notice upon entering the flight is the smell of mildew/mold and used blankets. The cabin was never cleaned since it's last flight (or perhaps since several weeks..who knows). Air India never restricts passengers from carrying huge bags to the cabin, so the overhead bins were filled up with bags of those who managed to board early. If you are lucky, you will get some space to keep your bag below your seat. The quality of food served was horrible. They will give you all those stuff that you shouldn't eat on a 17 Hour long flight (aloo,rajma etc). The lady who served tea/coffee reminded me of the chaiwalas in Indian trains. She was running around the cabin with a kettle of luke warm tea/coffee and was yelling "tea"..."chai"..."Kafeee"...with a typical "I hate my job" face and a fake smile that most Air India staffers have.
The only positive thing I can remember about this flight is the short 17 Hrs flight time (since this was a direct flight from USA to India). I would not recommend this flight if you are travelling with infants/small kids. Book it only if you are desperate to get to India as soon as possible.

title: "Miles to go"

title: Poor Equipment, Poor Food, Average Service
text:
We were a family of three, two adults and one kid. Our misery started from when we tried to check in online. The system failed multiple times, and finally we left that, frustrated. In Heathrow airport, all self check in counter was working except that of Air India. And there was big, haoti queue as one lady was trying to address all the passengers with their douments. She was helpful but the systems were not. So we waited for about half an hour before our turn came.

Next at the baggage counter, there was another drama. We though had three tickets, we had only one suitcase and a bag to deposit. The Suitcase wasn't oversized, but was weighing only 1.5 KG more than required. Whereas the bag was much lighter. We were way below in our permissible limits of 2*3*23 KGs, total weight o the bags were about 35 KG only. Still the lady at the counter, some Ms Sahana, having terrible attitude and even worse communication; make us open the suitcase and transfer a few things to the other bag. It was completely unnecessary and we seen this only as harrasment.

Next while boarding, they announced for families with kids to come forward in. Beleive me, there were only a handful of families and they made us walk the longest pathway! Everyone in the queue was loughing seeing the missmanagement. They made kids walk the longest!

The plane we entered was pretty old, and was stinking. The seats we offered, the headphone sockets were broken. So I had to give my seat to my wife so that she can enjoy the programs, and moreover, she has the same misfortune of having non operating audio while coming from Kolkata to London via Delhi. So this time I had to oblige her and I enjoyed (!) muted entertainment programs! The programs were stale - that is another concern.

I sincerely hope this was our last flight with Air India.

title: Worst Flight ever - even in Business Class
text:
FRA - DEL
DEL - BKK
And back

Due to fact that Air India is also Star Alliance member I booked flights in business class to Bangkok 

First of all the web checkin never worked!
Whether online with PC Browser nor IPhone App - after x attempts (and searching for eticket number somewhere in the booking reference) we only received "checkin confirmation" but no boarding pass.

Start in Frankfurt was ok - 3hours before flight checkin was open and we received tickets for both flight segments
Then access to Lufthansa Business Lounge - as good as always (some snacks, some drinks, possibility to take a shower - but no more massage seats!?)

First flight was good - nice staff, champagne before departure and tasty food.

After landing in Dehli first "shock" - you have to process security checks again! Although you just have connection flight and stay even in the same terminal!
Then access to Air India lounge: crowdy and loud!
Even you have may monitors with flight departure information a lady was walking around and yelling real loud "last call to Paris - last call to Paris" 
You were not able to rest or even sleep while this noise - and stop over time was extended from 5 to 6 hours as the next flight was delayed "due to operational reasons" - emails was sent 6 hours before....
After checking flightaware.com the last 10 days only 1 single flight was less than 10min delayed - and that on the home base airport!

Flight to Bangkok was with less friendly staff, no welcome drink before departure and although only 15 of 18 business class seats occupied my favorite dish with seafood was unavailable - not acceptable in business class!

Also no toiletry bag was provided - compared with flight before where you get toothbrush and paste, very well smelly Eu de Toilette and some hand and face Cremes and (a not even fit able at all) sleeping mask.
I assume this is only provided on long hauls >5h flight time.

Positive:
After landing in Bangkok we received priority pass for immigration and catches a taxi to downtown 30min after touchdown.

Flight back:
Planned take off 8:55am
Again noon before received flight status update - delayed 45min due to "operational issues"
So we could sleep longer, but stopover time was less than 1h - and bear in mind the security checks again!

Lounge access to Miracle Lounge right next to Gate - very very Nice, clean, spacious and very clean toilets (even for Asia)

Before boarding there was another security check right in front of the gate, where we had to leave our lighters - not allowed ... hm, thankfully we did not had our Zippos with us...

Takeoff was 9:55 so 1h later than planned.

Staff was little older than average but very friendly.
Even we had 1h later departure, arrival was in-time - positive.
But after landing the airport was confused and we had little waiting time for a free gate.... 

After then security check:
4 armed security officers looking around - 150 people waiting for check but only 1(!) officer is checking x-ray 
And don't forget some stamps!
Security check, Checkin at gate, checkin at airplane ... they seem to hire stamp people!

After all we managed to arrive at gate to Frankfurt right after boarding starts - but then still waiting 30min in plane (boarding completed) until rollout

Departure 30min late!

Airplane to Frankfurt was one of the older Dreamliner - out of order read lights, old-fashioned Toilet-Doors...
But staff was friendly

But again the favorite menu was not available anymore - not acceptable!
In a Business class with half occupied by Europeans Air India has to provide enough "non spicy" food!

Compared to flight FRA-DEL on this flight also no toiletry bag, even no pillow and no "nice blanket" for the sleep.

Overall also the onboard entertainment a little aged and not up-to-date:
Beside some English Hollywood movies many Bollywood movies and some inflight information.
No WiFi, no up-to-date inflight Information - my Dreamliner flight before with United was more modern here.

In a nutshell:
Even with business class the worst flights ever had:
- No online services at all for checkin
- Bad ground services at home base Dehli - I will never ever want to go to Dehli voluntarily!
- Flight Staff depending on flight and/or daily mude...
- Not a single flight segment was on-time (either departure or arrival) but you even know a day before. ;-)
Recommend to spend some 100. Of Euros more and fly other Star Alliance Members - Singapore Airlines or even Lufthansa

title: Avoid Ahmdabad
text:
In general Air India service has always been very good, even though sometimes you feel that you're being served by your mom. The upper class staff are usually the more mature staff, somewhat like on United Airlines.

Flight was via Amhdebad, UNFORTUNATELY. This is an airport I will want to AVOID. You arrive from Mumbai on what is supposed to be a domestic sector, then check out, and then go to the departure lounge and queue up for immigration, and boarding.

One disadvantage I have noticed about flying 787s is that they only open 1 door for boarding so EVERYONE boards at once and there is no priority for premium passengers, which is not a major issue really unless the queues are unruly

The Indians in Ahmedabad have figured this out to a science, and I have NEVER SEEN SO MANY WHEELCHAIR PASSENEGRS boarding on ANY flight IN MY LIFE, and I am on over 60 flights every year. They must have had in excess of 30 wheelchair passengers, so they breeze thru immigration and boarding in priority.

Yet upon arrival in Heathrow, I saw but 3 wheelchairs waiting for passengers outside the aircraft door.

So my suggestion would be to avoid Ahmedabad unless you want to use a wheelchair.

Flight from Ahmedabad to Heathrow was very good, and the seat goes flat and is comfortable for a god nights sleep. Inflight service was likewise very good, almost like you'd be treated as a guest in an Indian family home.

title: Surprisingly Very Bad Experience
text:
I am a big fan of Air India as it never disappointed me in the past. But yesterday I had a very bad experience with Air India.

I had booked flight from Surat to Mumbai and the expected time to arrive at Mumbai was 8.50. I had a connecting flight of Jet Airways from Mumbai to Bangalore @ 10.25 AM. There was a gap of 1 Hour 35 Minutes between these two flights which is more than enough.

The flight from Surat reached @ 9.40 to Mumbai and after that for 40 - 45 minutes the baggage did not come - due to this I missed my flight from Mumbai to Bangalore. There was no staff from Air India near the conveyor belt to listen to the passengers.  I was travelling with my 1.5 years old kid and I had to spend 5 hours @ airport with additional cost of 8000 for booking another flight.

When I spoke to the customer care representative @ Air India Airport Desk, they said as the flight to Bangalore was from Jet Airways, they can't help me book another flight.  They said they are only liable to drop me to Mumbai and 9.40 was the new arrival time, so they do not see any issue in that. When I said that the baggage did not come for 45 minutes, he said he can't do anything on that as well and asked me to escalate and do whatever I want to do.

I found the staff very unprofessional and did not care for what I had been through.

title: Horrible inflight experience
text:
I was travelling to USA with my family in the month of April 2017. Recently as USA President Donald Trump issued the notice of ipad, tab and laptop cannot be carried in the carry on bags as the cabin luggage like always and to be pur through the checked in baggages if the flights are coming via some muslim countries, so we had to book our flights with Air India. We thought the experience would be good but unfortunately it was not. It was our return trip flight. On our way to Chicago, the only usp was that the time period was real short. But the in flight services were horrible.They don't give eye masks, they don't give soft drinks or liquor other than one time in lunch. You have to walk down the whole aisle back of the plane to get hold of your drinks or juices. Even if you call an attendant, they don't come to attend you. The bathrooms were still okay to use till the end. On our way to Chicago the hault at Delhi was real short but on our return it was excruciatingly long. The flight to Kolkata from Delhi kept on postponing. We were supposed to fly at 8.15pm but it took off at 12am. With a kid sitting for so long on the sitting area near the gate was backbreaking. Plus strangely there was a confusion with my one of the luggages which very easily got cleared from Chicago Airport but not from Delhi airport. They confiscated lighters which were for gifts. They said that these are not allowed. But funnily in my other baggages few got cleared. Anyway they could have cleared it after checking them out. 
In our flight to Chicago and our way back to India....in both the flights the touch screens of the lcd were not working properly, in some the touch screen not working, in some the head gear didn't work,in some the remote didn't work so it became very boring mostly for my son. I actually had to see a movie without any sound just to pass time. Other than lunch dinner and breakfast there were no other food in the pantry.  Plus they didnt had what we booked for. We wanted three nonveg meal. But they gave us veg meal twice for one out of three. Inspite of saying that we don't need kids meal but need only proper meal they gave it which my son didn't eat at all. The domestic food was still better with good quality food. 
All in all the experience was real bad. I would never choose Air India as my next flight for my next destination. Its better to avoid this airlines and pack laptops and ipads in the checked in baggage.

title: The best business class service in spite of an unusual incident
text: I would rate my business class experience with this airline as my best in my 25 years of flying various airlines.  The reason is how the crew handled themselves, when an unusual emergency situation occurred over Turkish air space.  A passenger had a heart attack and the pilot had to land in Ankara airport to transport this passenger to the nearest hospital.   Ankara being a small airport and the aircraft being a 787 dream liner, the airline could not find a qualified engineer to qualify the aircraft to fly out of Ankara.  We were stranded for four hours in the aircraft, in the meantime the captain gave regular updates and the crews went out of their way to serve us and keep us in good humor.  The crew really seemed to care for the welfare of the passengers, even though I could hear some passengers screaming at the crew in the economy section.  The crew maintained calm and dignity.  Imagine doing that in an American airline.  The passengers would be royally shunted out and put in a Turkish prison.  The crew understood that the passengers were worried.  A certifying engineer had to be flown from India and we were put up in a business lounge in Ankara airport for almost 15 hours.   It was a travail, but the circumstances were beyond anybody's control.   The business class experience was wonderful.  The crew greeted us when we entered the cabin and showed us to our seats.  The food was good and we were given a set of pajamas.  The seat was pretty spacious and as big as the First Class ones in other airlines.  This is a business class experience I will never forget in a long time.  Kudos to Air India to maintain such high standards.  Other airlines should learn from this airline

title: Spare yourself the horror
text:
Coming from a person that has taken a decent amount of flights in my life a little piece of advice. DONT. 

We had been booked on an Air India flight to Hong Kong through Make My Trip. 
I guess because they offer the cheapest rate. 

We were flying to Hong Kong with a stop over at Delhi. The flight from Mumbai to Delhi had been delayed 4 times. Because of which we had to parade around Mumbai Airport multiple time. When the final delay happened the flight number was changed. 

We were not issued new boarding passes with the new flight number. They simply took the old boarding passes and hand wrote the new flight numbers on them. 

Due to this confusion with the flight numbers our luggage got on to the wrong flight. 
On FINALLY reaching Delhi airport when we were about to board the flight to HK they informed us that out luggage was not on the flight and they had no idea where it was. 

We were pretty surprised and had no idea how to deal with the situation. They told us to either board the flight without our luggage or miss the flight and pay for the next ticket out. We had no idea where our luggage was and had no other bags so we stood our ground and asked them to trace our luggage first.

I was exhausted trying to explain to them how the fault was theirs and my luggage had been misplaced by them. 

Me and my sister stood by the Air India counter for 5 hours tired and hungry while they ignored us. We stood by the counter and yelled and yelled calling for the manager multiple times but we were treated with an authentic Delhi spirit. 

Finally at 5 in the morning they offered to put up on the same flight the next day while they put us up in some shady hotel in delhi in the middle of the night while they still had NO IDEA where our bags were. 

All in all it was a really horrifying experience that no one should go through in their lives so just a piece of advise. Refrain from this airline.

title: On good wings
text:
in august 2016 i flew with air india from melbourne to frankfurt via new delhi. well, this is quite a long journey; and the prospect of having to hang around at indira gandhi international airport for 19 hours waiting for the connecting flight, could easily deter one from booking with air india, right? BUT: the airfare was so cheap that even with paying for a stay at the holiday inn express in terminal 3 (transit area!) it was a very reasonable - and because of the break - very enjoyable trip. 

the most important thing during the flight itself was (#1) excellent leg room. the second good thing (#2) was the very nice (although and as to be expected, a bit spicy) food. the third treat (#3) was the inflight entertainment selection - including yoga and indian cooking videos and a highly recommendable beautifully dramatized (abridged) audio version of mahatma gandhi's autobiography 'the story of my experiments with truth' (i wish i could find this particular one on the internet). # 4 would be that all flights were on time.

what i liked less - even as the airline seems to be very proud of it - is one feature of the B787 dreamliner: the dimmable windows instead of pull-down shutters. it is not that the feature itself is the problem, but that very early in the flight the staff already dimmed down the windows in the whole plane, no matter what time of the day! i found this highly annoying for two reasons: first of all, it messes even more with time (and related light/dark) differences. second, because i LOVE taking pictures during flights (and i am certainly not the only one to do so), i choose my window seat carefully in regards to being able to include a bit of the wing in some of the images to frame them, and most important, which side of the plane i would be able to witness a sunrise or sunset or see any beautiful mountain ranges, deserts, islands or other sights of interest in the areas over which we would be flying. now, when calling for the stewardess, she said she can certainly unlock my window dimmer so that i can regulate it myself, which saved my mood and allowed me to take breathtaking images once again... (on the longer leg of the return flight i sat in an over-crowded plane in a place where the dimmer happened to be broken... no pictures... but as this is not a main concern for most people, i rather focus on - and review - the good experience;-)

title: Delayed; Disgusting Interior
text:
I had high expectations for this segment of a round-the-world trip my husband and I were taking, based on my excellent history of flights with Air India years ago. Instead, this flight proved to be the worst of our journey. Indeed, I would put it near the bottom of all the airlines that I've been on during decades of flying.

The plane was scheduled to depart from Bahrain, en route to New Delhi India, at 11 p.m. Close to boarding time, we learned that there would be an hour's delay with no reason given. We went to wait in a small airlines lounge, which became uncomfortably crowded with standing room only. Eventually the delay got extended (still no explanation) and the plane finally departed at 2 a.m., three hours late.

As we boarded the plane, the condition of the exterior indicated no pride of ownership. The Airbus 319 had been sloppily painted, an indication of poor upkeep that I had never seen on any other carrier before. This situation did not improve inside. The Business Class cabin offered soiled seats that looked so unappealing that I wished I carried a towel with me to offer protection. As soon as I sat down, I noted the overflowing seat pockets on the back of the seats in front of us. Trash included old newspapers and candy wrappers. After the plane took off, I tried to recline my seat, only to find that it was broken.  

Extremely tired and definitely not hungry, both my husband and I declined the meal service, so I cannot comment on that. The plane made the strangest noises throughout the 3.5-hour flight, creaking, groaning and causing me to feel anxious, though I am usually a calm flier. As a result, I could not sleep. When I went to use the Business Class restroom, I noted the two flight attendants dozing. My shoes stuck to the restroom floor -- literally -- making loud crackling noises when I moved around, but that didn't awaken staff.

We arrived too late to make a connecting flight to Jaipur, which we had allowed almost 4 hours to do. So we waited for 3 hours in the airport at a wonderfully clean Starbucks with a pristine restroom before we were able to take to the air again.

title: sad for my national airline
text:
I had a very bad experience with AI, have narrated the complete story below (long read not necessary) my suggestions for fellow travelers would be not to rely upon Air India with tight schedules or connecting flights ... and even if you go for it and anything happens dont waste your energies on hoping some support or help .. rather plan for your own self 

thanks 

this horrified tale is my firsthand experience during our family trip (me, my wife and 4 ys old son) to hyderabad from jodhpur on 7th April. We had booked for IA flight jodhpur to mumbai AI 646 and connecting flight AI 965 from mumbai to hyd for 7th April. 

I had done the webcheckin for our seats even for the mumbai - hyd sector. when we reached at the jodhpur airport upon seeing the boarding pass we realised the onward flight from mumbai to hyderbad has been rescheduled to next day. (obviously no one informed us till then). Since my family was travelling to attend a family engagement in the evening of 7th, the next day flight made no sense hence we requested the AI executives at jodhpur to either cancel the tickets or make arrangements in another flight. The AI jodhpur did connect to their counterparts in mumbai and spoke with someone by name Stefan who assured that we shall be provided any alternate flight either AI or Jet for mumbai to hyd so that we can reach hyd by the evening hence should continue with our travel to mumbai and were asked to reach to the customer service desk in mumbai who would make necessary arrangements (a message was already sent) 

At mumbai we went to the customer service desk and we were guided to one Ms Rama, who after keeping us waiting for 15 min and upon our multiple requests spoke with someone and then issued us tickets and asked us to rush in towards the boarding gate no 50 as she said the flight was about to leave. We again checked in our bag and ran towards the boarding gates .. (since it was the international airport, we had to run towards the boarding gates as it was a very long distance. upon reaching the boarding gate no 50 the AI staff informed that the onboarding flight is for jeddah and the flight to hyd is yet to be announced and we were asked to wait. 

We sat near the boarding gates .. it was around 3.30 pm by then. After waiting for about an hour or so, and trying to figure out the flight schedule i just noticed that the boarding pass issued to me altough dated 7th of April has a flight timing of 04.00 hours which obviously refers to morning 4 am and thanks to the urgency shown by Ms Rama i didnt notice it when collected the boarding pass and assumed it for 4 pm evening. 

I immediately contacted an AI official near the boading gate Mr. Kumar and narrated our story, he tried to help us by making a few calls and then explained that the lady has done mistake in issuing the boarding passes and she has given you boarding passes for the same flight which is suppose to leave tomorrow (8th April) and erroneously the date mentioned is for today (7th April). He then asked us to go again to the counter and ask for a new boarding pass. 

we left, then were caught by the customs officers (rightly so) ... then again the whole story was narrated to them. They also sympathized, but said they cant let us go back from the immigration zone unless AI officers come here. They called AI officers ... after waiting for about 15-20 min AI officers turned up and then they explained the situation did some notings .. cancelled our boarding passes and then guided us again to the counters .... so again after a long walk back ... (by this time our baby had already gone restless and with lots of efforts we could manage to walk him back till the counters) 

We reached back to the counter at 6.00 pm and again met Ms Rama ... i told her my agony and complained who could she issue a wrong boarding pass .. for the same flight which is leaving tomorrow .. that too after informing you the complete story ... to my surprise inspite of apologizing for the mix up  and the problem faced by us, she started misbehaving and she said .... "i did what i was told to you and it is your mistake that you came to my counter, this is a domestic counter your ticket is in the international flight, you should have gone to the international counter"  .... i was stunned with the response and was so upset and wanted to give her back on her face for the rude, in-appropriate and irresponsible behavior .... may be my chivalry stopped me and the fact that i was perturbed by my child's agony that i decided just to move back and go to the international counter ( altough it did occur to me then, that may be the recent incident involving trashing of an AI staff by a politician for some seat issue could have been justified at some level - unfortunately in a democratic set-up only politicians have the luxury to react that way ... a common man can just suffer) 

i then moved to the international counter it was 6.15 by then. I met Mr. Kailash at the counter. He was a soft spoken person, listed patiently to the whole story and apologized for the inconvenience and promised us to help us, We waited for about 15-20 min and at about 6.30 pm he came back and said, i have spoken to my boss and also spoken with the duty manager (he named Mr. Revan and Mr. Gaikwad) and they have authorised him to book us into the next available flight, but since no other flight is available we can put us into the 10 pm flight (AI 050) for Hyderabad, i requested that i was promised any other airlines if AI is  not available so that i can reach hyd on time .. but Mr. Kailash mentioned that no other flights are available so you have the choice to either take this flight or take the morning flight and stay at mumbai. ... obviously our plan to attend the family function was gone atleast i was relieved that we can reach hyd by the night and i shall be able to attend a business conference at morning 10 am, hence agreed for the AI 050 flight.  ( i was a guest speaker at the Hyd RenewX - conference on renewable energy and was speaker participants in a panel discussion scheduled for 10 am on 8th April) 

Since my child was exhausted and so were we .. we decided to take the night flight and may be relax at the airport till then. I asked Mr. kailash to provide us atleast a lounge access so that we can relax till we waitup for the next flight. To which he refused as there is no such policy :-( ... anyhow we decided to manage things on our own and asked Mr. Kailash to issue boarding passes for the 10 pm flight and this is when we inquired about our checked in baggages which Ms Rama has taken from us earlier in the afternoon. 

Mr. Kailash inquired about the bags and he said ... he has already cordinated and the bags are being retreived and they will be put AI 050 aircraft so we should not worry and proceed towards security check. 

We took the boarding passes at about 6.50 and proceeded for the security check.. hoping that the things are now sorted and it was just a bad day ... to be forgotten.  

But AI had other plans for us, we reached at the boarding zone at about 9.30 pm but to our dismay flight for hyd was yet to be announced. We kept on waiting near the boarding gate hoping for some info from the officials as to the flight status ,,,,... together with several other impatient passengers we kept on inquiring but were getting no response on the flight for hyd. 

Finally we were told that the flight will leave at about 11 pm ...11 pm past still noting ,,,,,, finally the flight arrived and got scheduled at 00.15 hours for hyd. Already impressed with the service standards of AI, i asked the AI ground staff to confirm if my bags have been loaded in this aircraft..... to which the staff checked and assured me that your bags are already loaded. happy that finally the ordeal is over, we boarded the flight which might have flown out of mumbai around 1 am. 

We reached Hyd at 2 am and after scouting from belts to belts we finally realised that our bags are missing. ...at about 2.30 we approached the baggage section and they checked into the systems and said our bags were not loaded by mumbai and will arrive in the morning flight and will be delivered to your address. 

That was it, perhaps the only time when i must have lost my cool in the whole day. .... but it was of no use as the AI staff like any government servant have no sense of job responsibility neitto w morning you should call after 9.30 am .. (gave me a number to call at) and the person will tell you about the status. .... exhausted, helpless, disappointed and disparaged, with long faces we left the airport at 3.15 am for the 5 star hotel we booked and wasted the days booking money. 

Upon reaching the hotel i realised about my morning conference and how on earth was it possible to get business cloths by 9 am in morning to make it to the conference which again was other side of the town from where we were staying. Left with no option i wrote an email to the conference organizers notifying them with a last minute withdrawal and with all my apologies for the inconvenience ... yes a common man has the courtesy and courage to apologize, unlike these government servants. 

we checked into our room at 4.30 am and slept thinking how difficult the day was on us ... and how shattered our plans were by the end of the day. When someone would say .. now what wrong can happen ... the AI has few more to offer ... [ i dont know about anyone who is reading this, but i myself am getting tired writing about it any further, so would cut the further ordeal in short] 

after atleast 50 calls (including few people who stopped picking my phone and had to request hotel team to call on my behalf) and hearing to 5 different stories (obviously with false information) i could finally reach to one Mr. Sharat (040 66603056) at 4.30 pm in the evening and he told me all the people whom you have spoken so far have given you false stories about our baggages ... your bags have now left mumbai and will arrive here at hyd at 6 pm. title: The Never Ending Terror Of Air India
text:
I would like to start off by telling all readers what a disgrace Air India is to India, Indians and its passengers. I would like to share a recent experience that I had with Air India during my travel to India.

The nightmare started on Tuesday, April 18. I had come to India because of a sudden death in my family and I was scheduled to return to the US on April 18. My return flight was scheduled from Ahmedabad to Delhi and then Delhi to JFK, New York. Please note that this flight was full and consisted of about 300 passengers, majority of whom were elderly people (on wheel chairs) as well as numerous children. 

The level of incompetence showed by Air India during this flight is unimaginable. It is even more difficult to digest the fact that these people who are working for Air India represent India and Indians worldwide. What a shame! What a disgrace! Not just for the Air India team but the Indian government in general. Given that this is a “government” airline these fools thinks they can get paid without doing any work! 

The following events took place at the Delhi Airport on between Tuesday, April 18 and Wednesday, April 19:

1: 30 AM (Inside Air India Flight) - All passengers were boarded on to the flight as the flight was supposed to take off at 1:45 AM.  

2:00 AM (Inside Air India Flight) – The AC inside the flight was switched off. Current temperature in Delhi: 100 °C +. 

2:15 AM (Inside Air India Flight) - One of the captains announced that they were experiencing some delays due to “technical difficulties” and that we are expected to take off in 12 - 15 minutes.

2:30 AM (Inside Air India Flight) – Passengers are walking around the cabin, picking up magazines to use as a fan. Kids are screaming because of the heat, exhaustion and lack of sleep.

Between 2:30 – 3:00 PM (Inside Air India Flight) – One of the crew members announces that all passengers are going to have to get off the plane. 

All passengers stood up, got their carry on’s and waited patiently for the door to open. 10 minutes later, the same crew member announces “All passengers please get back to your assigned seats” and no other information… 

3:30 AM (Inside Air India Flight) - Once hour later the flight stood exactly where it was without any announcements or information from the crew members regarding the further delay. When I decided to approach one of the crew members asking what the problem was, their response “ We don’t know maam so we don’t know what to tell you”.

Between 3:30 – 4:00 PM (Inside Air India Flight) – Once again, one of the crew member announces that all passengers are going to have to get off the plane. All passengers stood up, got their carry on’s and waited patiently for the doors to open. Within a few minutes , the same crew member announces “All passengers please get back to your assigned seats” and ONCE AGAIN providing NO other information…

4:00 AM (Inside Air India Flight) -  Two and half hours into this nightmare as the heat became unbearable some of the passengers requested that Air India let people back into the terminal while they waited. One of the people requesting this was a mother carrying her child who was suffering with fever while another passenger was a diabetic patient. Air India refused this request and after some heated arguments with passengers they finally opened the airline door so the passengers could wait in the aerobridge area that connects the flight and terminal. See pictures. 

5:00 AM (Inside Air India Flight) -  FINALLY! They decided they were going to let people on to the terminal. Their reasoning for this – We are going to fly another plane to JFK so all passengers will have to change flights.

6:00 AM (Inside Terminal) – After almost five hours’ worth of wait, someone from Air India at the Delhi Airport tells a handful of passengers that this flight is being CANCELLED. After being asked by several people to SPEAK UP and INFORM ALL PASSENGERS OF THE CHANGE this man finally made an announcement. 

Reasoning for cancellation – the crew’s shift is over and they have left so there is no one who can fly the plane (Are you serious?). The next flight will depart to JFK today evening at 5PM AND in the meantime all passengers are being taken to a hotel WHICH IS ONE HOUR AWAY FROM THE AIRPORT (Again, Are you SERIOUS?!?). All passengers will need to COLLECT THEIR LUGGAGE and CANCEL THEIR IMMIGRATION to they can take the evening flight.

6:30 AM (Delhi Airport) – I have decided I am not going to a random hotel. Given the lack of disorganization that Air India has shown tonight I do not trust that the evening flight will depart. I decided to purchase an Emirates ticket for a flight to JFK which was departing at 11:00 AM instead. 

After cancelling my immigration I asked an Air India representative what the process was if I wanted to get back bags back. She asked me to go upstairs to the second floor to the Air India counter and ask them for my bags.

When I reached the Air India counter on the second floor, the man at the counter said he cannot help me and that I need to go to the baggage check in counter for Air India and they will provide my bags. So I go there. The female staff at this counter tells me “I don’t know anything about this flight”. Then I ask a third person and explain my situation that the flight was cancelled and I have another flight at 11:00 AM, whose check in will close at 10:00 AM so I need my bags. This man finally tells me that he can get my bags but it’s going to take them 4 HOURS. By now it is 7:00 AM and my check in with emirates was going to close at 10:00 AM leaving me 3 hours to get my bags back. 

Given my lack of time, the male staff I was speaking with calls a female staff to assist. Once again, she gives me the same excuses that the other person did. By this point, I have had no sleep, no food and no rest. I tell her “I don’t care that the process says you need 4 hours, I only have 3 hours and I don’t want to miss my next flight so PLEASE atleast TRY to get my bags”. At this she says “Maam if you don’t care then I can’t help you” and WALKS AWAY! 

ARE YOU SERIOUS? Where do these people get SO much ego from? Aren’t we as Indians supposed to be kind hearted? Aren’t we supposed to help each other in need? What do these staff members get paid for? Why do they even get a salary? And why are they not fired already? Oh! That’s right – it's a government agency where it is almost impossible to fire people. So here we are, stuck having to deal with absolute IDIOTS!

Finally, after repeatedly pleading to the other staff member one of the on floor managers came to me. He said they would try his best to get my bags and takes my passport. Given how frustrated I was by this point I didn’t think twice before giving him my passport.  BIG MISTAKE – DO NOT GIVE YOUR PASSPORT TO ANY AIR INDIA STAFF MEMBERS! 

This floor manager gives my passport to one of his workers and sends him to retrieve my bags. 

8:30 AM (Air India Counter) – Can you check to see if they founds my bags? Their reply – yes, he is completing paperwork and will be back in an hour.

9:00 AM (Air India Counter) – Can you check to see if they are on their way? Their reply – yes, he is on the way.

9:30 AM (Air India Counter) – Can you check to see if he is almost here, my check in closes in 30 minutes? Their reply – yes, he is almost here.  

9:45 AM (Next flight check in closing at 10:00 AM) – The floor manager calls the guy who is out retrieving my bags. The on floor manager tells me “Looks like they have the wrong bags”…. 

This was the moment I lost all faith, in this Airline, their staff and the Indian Government! I think at this point it is ok to say that it’s not the individual agencies who are 100% incompetent. It is the Indian Government who is incompetent. 

9:55 AM (Air India Counter) - NOW, the on floor manager tells me – why don’t you take the emirates flight, we will send your luggage on the next Air India flight to JFK. Again, ARE YOU KIDDING ME? If this was an option, why did you not let me do this when I had initially asked if my bags could be delivered directly to JFK? Oh my goodness, I mean the level of STUPIDITY Air India!

10:00 AM (Emirates Counter) – Emirates was ready to close their check in counter. I pleaded and they agreed that they would wait 10 more minutes for me. By now you must be wondering – well the guy fetched the wrong bags so what were you still waiting for? 

Well, MY PASSPORT! 

While I am pleading emirates to keep their counter open, the Air India guy is on his phone saying that we cannot find the guy that has your passport…

Readers: Do you feel the anxiety? And the frustration? And the Anger by now?

10:15 AM (Emirates Counter) – The Air India Idiot who had my passport finally arrived and Emirates was kind enough to let me board the flight!! 

For those who watch hindi movies – you know how in patriotic movies when they show a long time Indian prisoner being released from Pakistan gets to come home to India he drops to the ground with happiness. That was how I felt when my flight landed in JFK…

P.S: After returning home, Air India called 4 days later telling me that my bags would be delivered at night between 11:30 PM and 1:30 AM on a work night. When we called to ask for a refund, they told us to follow up with the Ahmedabad office!!! The nightmare just DOESN’T END!!!

For all readers / travelers considering Air India: Please, please, please, unless you have no other options please travel by a better airline instead of using Air India. My husband and I had no choice when we booked our flights, we booked the first flight to India upon receiving news of a death in our family.

The flight costs were reasonable but that's where the good points end. The flight attendants were surly and looked so fed up, on both flights. The worst part of was the lack of any system for boarding flights. As soon as boarding was announced, there was a free for all with passengers shoving and pushing despite have a designated seats and boarding cards. The airline staff made no effort to control the boarding and stood looking bored and disinterested.  Has to be the worst airline I've ever experienced.

title: Fly them if you must.
text:
Flew on AI 433 which is on a vintage(At least 15 years old) A320. 

Check-in was fine (I'm a *A Gold card so I was able to use the business queue in DEL). Lounge facilities were basic but more than adequate for a domestic flight. 

Boarding was a complete mess (as is the case in India) I had to force my way to the front of the queue for Priority boarding 

The aircraft was unbelievably warm throughout the flight. Several passengers complained about the cabin temperature and were told that there was nothing that could be done. My seat mate in 4B noticed that the arm rest was wobbly and when he attempted to put it down for take off, the entire armrest just collapsed. When he told the flight attendant about it, he was just simply told 'alright'. 

Catering on this nighttime flight was fine. You get a full vegetarian dinner (rice, dal, paneer). It's much better then what you would get on any US carrier. 

Lower your expectations and fly them if you must

title: No customer service
text: Air India was unbelievably inept and uncaring. The flight had to make an emergency landing in Ankara to evacuate an ill passenger. Nobody had problems with that. It was the right thing to do. However we ended up staying Ankara for 24 hours and received NO updates or information from Air India. We were herded like cattle into a narrow and cold departure lounge, guarded by airport security. Most of us were dressed for the heat of Mumbai, not the chill of an Ankara winter night. We were not allowed to leave this area, even those of us who did not need visas for Turkey. The Air India staff disappeared completely (taken to hotels) while we passengers were treated like sub-humans. The Turkish airport authorities provided us with food and they kept the washroom clean but Air India DID NOTHING. They did not even explain the reason for the delay. One of my travel companions was able to call a highly-placed relative in India who made a few calls and managed to find out what was happening and why we were delayed. This second hand information at least gave us some understanding of the situation. Air India should fire their entire communications staff and send all remaining staff to a communications course taught by people who understand that passengers do have some rights. This was a debacle from beginning to end. (And needless to say, AI offered no compensation to those of us who missed connecting flights, had to stay in hotels when we arrived in Mumbai, or suffered other inconveniences.) I am a very experienced traveler but this really does rank as my worst airline experience ever.

title: First time Traveling to Europe with Maharaja
text:
In spite of being  a very frequent overseas traveler, I have never tried Air India and always opted for Emirates , Etihad or Lufthansa. During my current trip to Germany on 22nd Apr'17,  I opted for Air India little reluctantly and out of compulsion. The first leg of the travel was with flight AI 21 from Kolkata to Delhi. Check in was smooth and fast luggage was booked directly to Frankfurt. Immigration was also done at Kolkata, which is always a better option than at Delhi. Post immigration , I was invited to the Travel Club Lounge for a quick breakfast. I selected seat 2B an aisle seat. Seat configuratuon was 2 2 2 . It was quiet spacious in the cabin with only 18 seats. Flight departed on time. It was a B 787 Dreamliner aircraft. The aircraft surprisingly looked worn out considering the fact that B 787 is a new aircraft. Welcome drink Virgin Mojito was very refreshing. Sandwiches and light brunch was served. Presentation of food  was below par for Business Class. Coffee was served in crockery but instead of cutlery, cheap disposable plastic spoon was given. These small things make a lot of difference. Flight landed after 15  minute delay and I had to rush to Gate 13 which was quiet far. There was chaotic crowd at the transfer security check thanks to Delhi Airport. I manged to board my connecting flight 131 just on time. This was also a 787 Dreamliner. Flight was full. I had seat 1D an aisle seat of my choice. Interior of the aircraft is below par as compared to its Indian Peer Airlines or other European or Middle East Airlines. Seats was full flat but not to my expectation as a frequent business passenger. There was extreme lack of privacy in the seat alignment. Absolutely no plan to create storage of small acessories. Menu card was given. But no  separate wine list in Business Class. So shocking. Flight took off on time. Non alcoholic welcome drink was offered. I went for coconut water. Flight entertaient system offered choice of Indian and western movies. Toilet in Business Class also looked sub standard to me. Lunch was served after take off. There was good choice in main course, I opted for Prawn Newburg served with persley potatoes and vegetables. Wine selection was very substandard. I asked for white wine with my prawns but they had ordinary Chaddonney and Bourdeaux. Quality was not upto the mark. I had to ask for comfort kit which was supposed to be given normally. While sleeping good duvet was made available. Before landing light snacks of kebabs and sandwiches was served. I ended my food with a glass of cognac. Flight landed on time and luggage was at the carousel before I reached there.
      To sum up my experience , first with negatives : 1. Aircraft had pretty ordinary interior with compromised passenger comfort. Looks to be the cheapest within 787 class 2. Lack of privacy in the seat. They should have provided retractable privacy curtain 3. Food is not up to business class standard, presentation very poor 4. Worst choice of wine and alcoholic beverages 5. Toilet is very ordinary 6. No in-flight duty free shopping. 6. You do not feel of class and real business class flavor.
  Now with positives : 1. Latest N787 Dreamliner aircraft 2. Good connectivity 3. Lands at T1 which is close to train station 4. Cheaper than its competitors by at least 10-15% 5. Through Check in and immigration at Kolkata.
My conclusion : Do take if you get at good bargain. You have to compromise real business class feel that you get in Emirates or Lufthansa or other middle east or European airlines.

title: Review of Delhi-Rome and Milan-Delhi flight
text:

The choice of drinks is good and the best part is that they do not even uncork the wine bottles so that they can carry them home. The only complaint is that the red wine was Sula, an Indian drink. title: Where to begin?
text:
I flew with my husband and two kids (7 and 9) on the direct flight from JFK to New Delhi.  This is a 15 hour flight and we were counting on the entertainment system to help pass the time.  I should have known something was wrong when my daughter's seat's screen would not respond to touch and three of the buttons on the handset were missing.  This meant there was no way to change the volume!  Anyway we somehow we both managed to start a movie.  For both of us, after five minutes, and the system would reset making us start again over and over till we gave up after asking the stewardess for help three times.  She claimed to have rebooted the system twice, to no avail.  My husband's handset was completely dead. The staff, though polite, was helpless and laughing at the absurdity of the situation with me.  I heard the stewardess tell the lady behind me that her system was not working eitehr.  15 hour flight, people!!
My tray table was broken and at an angle that it could not hold my food tray without sliding off.  If you want an alcoholic beverage with your meal, your only option is wine and they don't offer it, rather you have to know and ask for it.  
On the way back, the stewardess actually told me to come to the back and get wine if I wanted it.  In 20 years of flying internationally, I have never been told that.  On the 15 hour flight back, the restrooms were not cleaned once.  They were filthy, in disarray, with supplies thrown all over the place.

title: Not impressed
text:
We had booked our flight with Air India from Goa to Mumbai departing on flight AI84, Wednesday 1st March at 22.35. We were then connecting with Air India flight to Bangkok which was departing on 2nd March at 01.45.

We were able to check in online the day before, so all was good and we arranged for the taxi to pick us up at 20.30 to take us to the airport, so everything was ready. We were going to enjoy our last day on the beach and have an early dinner there before setting off.

About 10 o'clock, morning of the 1st, we got an email and a phone call from Air India informing us that the Goa to Mumbai flight was delayed by 1 hour and we would be departing at 23.30. They also advised that we might not make the Bangkok connecting flight. There is only 1 Air India flight a day to Bangkok.

We phoned Air India back, 45 minute call, trying to change our flight to an earlier departure from Goa. We got seats on flight AI 662, leaving Goa at 18.45, but we had to be at the Airport by 16.30 to claim the tickets, or we would loose them. This meant hanging around Dabolim airport for 2 hours. It was important that we made the connecting onward flight as we had booked a taxi and paid for a taxi to collect us and we had paid for the hotel.

The boarding went smoothly as the plane pushed back 10 minutes early and was in the air on time. But due to congestion at Mumbai we were slightly late landing there.

The seats were ok, suitable for a short haul flight and leg room reasonable, the cabin crew did not appear very interested.

We were served a snack, which was awful, it consisted of 2 slices of dry bread with a slice of sweaty cheese inside and a small bottle of water.

Once in Mumbai airport we had to hang around for 5 hours, not in our original plan, Air India did not offer us use of a longe or anything for the inconvenience and disruption, in fact they did not even apologise.

Overall opinion of Air India, not a lot. We also think that the original flight was cancelled as it never appeared on the flight information board in Mumbai.

Thursday morning 2nd of March and we started boarding our Air India flight AI330 to Bangkok at 00.45, an hour before we were due to take off. Despite this early boarding we were 20 minutes late in departing, think they were waiting for connecting flights as people boarded very late.

title: March 9, Delhi to SFO Direct Service, devoid of "Service" !
text:
AI 173, March 9 DEL-SFO

WOW! Where do I start as to how the flight was:

Let me begin with the good part - It is a direct flight - very convenient;  and it  was mostly on time - both departure and arrival . But that is where the good part ends in my experience.

a) The cabin becomes a dust bin littered with stuff within first couple of hours. You can only imagine the toilet facilities - if they can be called facilities. The crew apperas oblivious to it - they  do nothing about it where I have seen other airline crew making sure isles and even toilets are clean during the flight. Perhaps AI should fine people for littering inside the plane! They will make enough money to become profitable! 

b) Flight attendant service was non existent. My isle was served by this one exceptional person - exceptionally RUDE on so many dimensions that is - Makrant Desai - condescending - like when I asked for help to bring down my bag from the overhead bin (way too high for me to reach) when I needed to take out a medicine he told me repeatedly  I should keep it under my seat. I can only surmise, so I would not bother him again. This person exhibited total lack of understanding of his job that is rooted in “serving” his customers. 

c) I was a bit sick on this flight so I didn’t eat any of the meals they served. You’d expect the crew to try  to help make the passenger comfortable, just a bit - but they had nothing to offer!  Also between meals during snack service, they put out a big trash bag in the food area which got filled quickly with discarded stuff, and parents were having tough time keeping their small children out of that. They really should not be doing that - its a a safety issue.  Trash bin should be something children can't get into easily.   

It is rather unfortunate the airline PM Modi so proudly stated would bring direct service to travelers between SFO and the Indian Capital is so devoid of “service”.  Their crew does not really extend one morsel of care - and for the long flight that it, their food service seems like a “fast food service”. Crew dishes out instructions - get in your seats, open your tray tables .. so that they have to spend no time putting your tray on it and move on asap.

The fact that you can get non-stop from point A to point B has its merits but I for one value some degree of service and care if I am going to be on it for 15 long hours. So I only hope that I never have to get on this one again.

title: Delays are common
text: I was to fly from from Bhopal to Mumbai early this week. The flight which was to take off at 9.50 pm actually took off around midnight. Very frustrating indeed.

title: Lost baggage
text: I took Air India flight 102 (NY-Delhi) on Monday 2/20  arriving on time on Tuesday 2/21.  However, my suitcase did not. I filed a claim and was told it would take 24-48 hours to arrive. Since I was on a tour going to multiple cities, I gave AI reps my itinerary and the hotels I will be staying at. Also, the phone number of my tour guide. On Thursday morning,  2/23,  while en route from Delhi to Jaipur we received a call that the bag is at Delhi airport. Friday night at 9:30pm while at dinner, a courier came and said he had my bag in his car. However, I would have to pay 1550 rupies (about $20) for the delivery. If I refused to pay he would return my bags to Jaipur airport. He did not accept credit cards and he did not have a receipt to show I paid. My anger is why did I have to pay for the delivery of my bag that was mishandled by Air India?

title: Avoid Air India
text: Business Class on Air India is terrible.  Recently I flew their nonstop from San Francisco to New Delhi and back again.  15 or 16 hours in a comfortable seat would be a challenge. Some of the cabin crew were OK; others were surly and unhelpful.  The food wasn't bad, but couldn't compensate for the overall experience of being in a rundown neighborhood. title: AI 112 and AI 111
text:
I am a fan of Air India, despite the horror stories I have heard from all different sources. Whenever I go to India, I make a deliberate effort to go with Air India. Primary reasons are relatively comfortable seating, good delicious food and plenty of check in luggage. And yes, they are definitely the best priced so, this is it.

Being an avid fan, I was very surprised on my recent trip to Delhi from London and back. They have replaced Boeing 787 with a very old 777, so the entertainment screens leave much to be desired, the seat backs are cracked and the headphones they provide sometimes are broken (this was the first time). The flight was full and overbooked (perhaps both ways but certainly on the way back DEL-LHR).

For some reason, I am a firm believer in Air India and will continue to use them for rather parochial reasons, but I feel, with a little bit of effort , they can save money and make customers happy. 

I must say that I have a bit of a bias for Air India . I have been subjected to Jet Airways, KLM, Lufthansa, Virgin, Gulf, Emirates, SAs (when they used to fly to India), 
I love SAS but they dont fly from Copenhagen to Delhi anymore, rather unfortunate.

I seriously want Air India to be the best carrier for India !!!

title: Prop plane
text:
I usually fly with Jet Airways between Jaipur and Delhi, as I'm not a great fan of Air India.  However, on this occasion, the Air India flight times better suited my needs.

The plane was the inevitable prop plane, used so often on these short routes.  However, I was very pleasantly surprised with the interior of this plane.  Unlike the fabric covered seats I have experienced on other Air India flights (which to me always look dirty and smell), this plane had lovely leather seats.  And the interior was very clean - the carpet almost looked new.  I declined the onboard snack as all that was on offer was a coleslaw sandwich, and it's not really something that is to me liking - what a shame Air India isn't able to match its rival Jet Airways' non-veg offering too.

Overall, this was probably the best ever Air India flight I have taken.  What a shame all the airline's plane interiors aren't like this one.

 The 2hr Flight was good no turbulence,Cabin crew were friendly and smiling to passengers..Water was not freely passed around until dinner service or you had to request some.We were seated in the middle of the plane so had the dinner trolleys coming from the front and rear and of course when they got to me which was an arduous wait , they did not have my preferred Non-Veg dish..the stewardess was apologetic but could do little else so had to settle for a Veg dish which I must admit was tasty and later compliment the Cabin Crew on this , as I was a bit grumpy- (and made them know it) from the slow dinner service and having no choice  of a preferred meal... but after I complimented the food they offered me another Veg dish ..I declined as a matter of courtesy ..We landed in Delhi about 15-20min later than scheduled ....but overall slightly "above average"  flight ..musta been the food ...and pleasant cabin crew

title: Just awful.
text:
One star is generous. My flight was delayed, which initially wasn't a problem. We were put up in a lovely hotel. But that's where the good news ends. Nobody seemed to know what was happening at any given time and we were shuttled around from place to place with no information at all. In the end, the flight was delayed by 30 HOURS. I had a connecting flight to Nepal which I consequently missed, and had to wait 15 hours in Delhi for this flight to be rearranged. This meant that i was almost 48 hours late to my project in Nepal that I had paid a great deal of money for. Once on the flights, it was uncomfortable and the staff were cold and unwelcoming. 

But my horrible experience doesn't end there. I am within my rights to contact the airline regarding compensation from Air India following my experience. I am entitled to this compensation. I first contacted the airline at the end of OCTOBER. It is now nearly the end of February and I have only received one email from Air India, despite them having received about 6 from me encouraging them to sort this mess out quickly. Im not impressed. 

My advice: DON'T DO IT.

title: Terrible flight on Flight number 101 and 102
text: I have traveled Air India Flight 101 and 102 several times since direct flight between New York and New Delhi was started. But my recent experience (Jan-Feb 2017) was so bad that I would not recommend Air India and these flights anymore. Since purchase of these planes for long routes, their seats and entertainment systems are not maintained or serviced at all in the economy class. Seat cushions are compacted down and metal parts of the seats are exposed (please see attached pictures). I paid extra US$50 for each seat per flight (101 and 102, seat number 41 A and C). On both flights entertainment system did not work at all. Crew staff cannot fix hardware failure (I understand that it is not their job). Crew told us that they complained to ground staff to fix entertainment system but nothing happens. After Flight 102 on Jan 27, I personally went to an Air India Manager at the IGI airport to complain but instead of taking any action, he asked me to write it on Air India complaint box. When I asked for a refund of extra charge of $50 x 2  for two seats (41 A and C), he refused to talk to me. Plane was dirty. Bathrooms were not cleaned once during 15 hour flight (from Delhi to New York). Food was just OK; please do not expect what you used to get 7 – 8 years ago. Safety violations were everywhere, please see attached pictures. Pilot of flight 101 February 18 was inexperienced, In a perfect clear day without rain, snow or wind, pilot almost crash landed a left side tilted plane. It scared everybody on the plane.

title: Ohh how Air India it is?

title: Needs Improvement !!!
text:
I flew on Air India from Delhi-London-Delhi in Feb 2017. On the flight to London, it was a new plane and it was a comfortable trip (except for the fact that while checking in the Air India representative didn’t know where the Business class passengers were supposed to check-in from and sent me to the Economy class counter to board). 
On the flight back from London to Delhi, there was a really old plane. My seat did not recline and when I was asked to change seats, the new seat has a cushion missing so one was sitting on the metal frame. I was then asked to return to my original seat and the crew got it to recline to approx. 110-120 degrees instead of 180 degrees.  There were 2 washrooms in business class and in one, there was no water and in the other, the flush wasn’t working. I was left standing with soap on my hands and the crew had to wait for instructions from the pilot (!!!) to allow passengers to use the wash rooms in the front of the flight. The crew seemed to need instructions for everything from a senior staff member (there wasn’t any empowerment there)!! The crew was hard working but handicapped by the red-tapism it seemed. There was tape holding pieces of the plan together near the seats.  Breakfast was a croissant and bun and fruit. I would be hesitant flying Air India in the future due to the possibility of an old plane being used for a flight.

text: Failed on line booking. Bank account debited. Air India claim to have sent refund. Never received even after 2 months. All details sent at least 20 times. Be warned....

title: If I could have given this airline zero stars - I would have.
text:
We were 3 passengers trying to travel from Mumbai to Goa on 5th October 2016.  Our Air India flight was delayed, then delayed again, then cancelled completely.  We were allocated onto another later flight - then it was delayed too.  We were treated like a total irritation to the airline - just a nuisance - no customer respect or good service shown to us at all.  When we eventually got to our hotel in Goa, many hours later than expected, the management there told us that Air India is always like that, and we should have selected a different airline.
I wrote an e-mail to Air India to complain when we got back home to Scotland.  Then I sent another e-mail ... and another ... and another.  I have now been waiting 4 months and I have sent a total of 23 e-mails, but they have not dealt with my complaint.  They keep on acknowledging my communication in a standard message and apologising for the inconvenience, but they have done nothing to compensate me for a truly dreadful experience.
My advice to you - avoid Air India at all costs.  Shockingly bad.

title: The worst airline I've flown on
text:
This is by far the worst airline I've flown on. My companion's seat was broken and wouldn't adjust; the food was concealed, cold and inedible; service non-existent. Discipline on safety procedures less than any flight I have ever been on (and I've flown Air Mozambique which takes some beating for scariness, and Turkey's Air Pegasus where they laugh if you ask for a glass of water.) title: Air India Snapshot
text: India's national airline does not leave a good impression with passengers. Plenty of things are left to be desired/improved upon, from the cleanliness, to the staff service, to the conditions of on-board electronics, to flight timings. The plus points are that the cost of flying is cheap, the staff isn't stingy with food/beverages and the flight landings are smooth.

title: Improving with every next flight which I took
text:
This was a good trip from Air India. 1.5 hours journey. Food provided during the flight was one complaint point which I had in the past and now that is improving. 
Landing and Take off was smooth and thus an overall good trip.

title: Book it if you only want a cheapest ticket
text: Surprised that it has managed to get into the Star alliance. The over head luggage cabin was taped. The plane seemed like it has not been cleaned in a 1000 years as there was a pungent smell as soon as i boarded the flight. The air hostess were ugly to say the least and looked unhygienic. The tray was broken and it was tilting towards one side. The staff did not have any sense of customer service.  They were  rude. The only positive is that they have a higher luggage allowance. Please take a medicated bath once you fly this Air India.

title: Air India - an experience!
text:
My feelings and I flew with Air India to Delhi, we booked these flights as they were affordable, direct, and to be honest we didn't review beforehand! 

The flight and airline itself was fine - a bit chaotic (mainly the other passengers creating chaos)... at times it was even comical! 

We seemed to be the only passengers able to locate our allocated seat without confusion, which was odd, as each ticket provides a seat number - understanding culture differences we though perhaps this is due to the numbers. 

During the flight we were comfortable, had a selection of in house entertainment with some good films! The screens are dated and quite unresponsive and slow! If you accidentally stop a film halfway through good luck getting back to the same point! 

Halfway through the flight a lady tried to climb over me, I was a bit confused, it turns out she wanted to get to the seat next to me - I couldn't work out why she didn't ask, or get my attention first, she then continued to lean on me and cough in my ear for the remaining 6 hours of the flight, and use my USB port etc.. (they provide USB!).. that's a plus! 

The staff were ok, but didn't really see the need to see to the western girls (us) needs / requests, we usually had to ask about 3 or 4 times... there was no logical order to serving the customers, it seemed favourable. 

The toilets could have been cleaner, however did provide mouthwash (random)...

title: Embarrassment of an airline
text:
Terrible website: 
clunky interface, not user friendly, multiple loading errors and reminiscent of websites built in the early days of the internet. In fact, I had so much trouble on the website that I ended up using a third party website to book my tickets.

Understaffed, unorganized and inefficient airport staff:
The check-in process is ridiculously long. I have consistently had to arrive at the airport (in India) up to 4 HOURS in advance, just because of how slow Air India check in is. It is almost always understaffed and somehow each customer takes upwards of 10 mins just to check in. I remember once when the line was so long it stretched back to the airport entrance, and instead of more staff being recruited to help - staff were actually leaving their counters!

Unreliable in-flight entertainment system:
The selection is not bad and the screen size is good. If only it worked. In the majority of Air India flights I have taken, the the system is either malfunctioning, unnecessarily slow or simply not working. Once when I realized the nobody's screens were working, I asked the air hostess to reset the plane's entertainment system (a common practice in most airlines when the system doesn't work), and she had no idea what I was talking about and how to go about doing it; I and the rest of the passengers spent the entirety of a 7 hour flight without in-flight entertainment.

You know it's a sad situation when a country's budget airlines (IndiGo, Spice Jet) are leagues better than it's flag carrier and largest international airlines (Air India, Jet Airways).

title: AIR INDIA NEVER AGAIN
text:
Last November my daughter & I had just enjoyed holiday in India  during the Diwali Festival  - fantastic
The pollution & smoke from fireworks during the festival gives  many people  respiratory problems. Many people on the Air India flight were coughing which was to be expected, - but two women behind (our friend was sitting next to them)  were coughing & then spitting onto the floor. Surely this is not acceptable. 
  
On arrival, our luggage was  damaged mine a soft cover was bent/twisted  but not torn.  My daughter's expensive Samsonite hard cases were ruined.. Both cases had multiple cracks right through the shell & handle, they cannot be used any longer. My daughter reported the broken cases immediately, forms filled & photos taken and the all important ref number & contact phone number for her to call. 
She tried the contact number many times during our stay in Sri Lanka & got the run around. She was told to meet an Air India employee at Colombo airport before departure.  This caused problems as we needed to check in & the Air India representative had to be called many times, he eventually turned up with two other men. They really didn't care when they looked at the damage cases and were certainly not going to take responsibility for the damage. Then an offer of $75 for the damage. A very uncomfortable discussion went on -   No, their  boss Lady could not come she was in her city office (we had 2 hours till the plane departed) - They withdrew their $75 offer & told us to go to the Air India office in our home city of Perth. Where is the office?  we asked - They came back & said there was no Perth office -  we should go to the Sydney or Melbourne office. - "Do you know how faraway we live from Sydney?"
Clearly these employees were not  the people that  we should have had to deal with.  They appeared to have no managerial or customer service skills.  My personal feeling is because we were women, these AI employees had no intension of doing anything & were stalling. Knowing that no further face to face discussion could take place after we left the country, and the report would never be followed up.  Since returning home my daughter has phoned the Air India office in Colombo - you guessed it no result.  
Air India will not suffer because of my review - as they have so many people traveling between Delhi & Colombo. 
Surely someone at Air India  must be responsible for customer care & service.

title: An ideal airline to fly anywhere, for short duration of flights, especially to Middle East
text:
Although I do not have any experience of Air India on long haul flights as yet, the short flights to Asian countries and the Middle East are very comfortable with Air India. Their 3-4-3 seating, meals they offer, in-flight entertainment, their short flying timings as against other carriers, and a beautiful take-off & landing are just a few of its attractions.
IT IS ABOUT TIME WE STOP REMEMBERING AND LIVING IN THE PAST AND INSTEAD NOW LIVE IN THE PRESENT - THE NEW SERVICE QUALITY OF AIR INDIA.

title: Very comfortable flight
text:
Some time before the flight, I received a text message advising me to reach four hours before the scheduled departure due to congestion at the terminal. I did but it was unnecessary as the check-in took very little time. The wait in the Air India lounge was however very comfortable. 
The flight took off on time. The cabin was spacious and comfortable. The seats were wide with plenty of leg room. The crew was very helpful. 
There was a plenty of choice in beverages. The food, though rather bland, was good. It was a non-stop 15-hour flight but I had a sound sleep as the seat stretched almost to a flat bed. In short, it was a very comfortable flight.

title: Chicago Delhi business class
text: For those reading such negative reviews of Air India long haul, here is a positive one. Yes, the 2-3-2 seating configuration in business class isn't as modern as the pods but it is just fine.  Seats are wide and there is plenty of room to stretch out and move about.  The front cabin is three rows and this is preferable to the rear cabin in business class which is 2 rows, the middle section reserved for flight crew. Flight left on time, and lunch was served.  We chose the western meal of salmon which was pretty good.  Service was friendly and competent and attentive.  After lunch, lights go down and people read or watch entertainment until sleep time.  Entertainment is not as broad ranging as Air Canada for example but there was enough to watch, some new, some classics to amuse oneself.  Breakfast is served 2 hours before arrival and that too was just fine. Seats fold down to almost flat but contour of the cushions does not make for a smooth surface.  Folded down, seat is about 65 inches long meaning feet stick over the end and there is no foot extension.  Not different from my experience on ANA long haul.  Not a full bed but sleep is still manageable. Overall, not an unpleasant experience as many have suggested for 14 hours in the air.

title: Miserable facilities, equipment, legroom, service
text: My wife and I flew from New Delhi to NYC yesterday on Air India--and, as in our outbound flight several weeks ago, were most disappointed.  The reasons: (1) Equipment: On both the outbound and return flights the lights and/or tv screen didn't function properly.  (On the return, it was both lights and tv.)  Oddly: someone sitting three ahead of us had a controller that controlled our overhead lights--although the tv didn't work any way at all.  If this equipment doesn't work, what about the plane's flight controls???  (2) Seating: despite our having selected seats and had the assurance on our etickets that we would be assigned these seats, we were assigned different--and less attractive--seats when checking in.  And we checked in quite early--among the first passengers to do so.  (3)  Food: in brief: awful: The smaller meals were dreadful: doughy rolls with no cheese, an omelette hard as a rock, etc.  Worse yet was the main meal: a chicken curry loaded with chilis but in which no masalas were evident.  This gives Indian cuisine, which we adore, a terrible name!  (4) It is incredibly difficult getting frequent flyer credit for flying with AI.  We had an account that expired and couldn't renew it.  And enrolling again is terribly hard: one needs to send a photo and much other information.  We have frequently flyer accounts with numerous airlines and no come close to making it so hard to enroll in their program.  AVOID THIS AIRLINE IF POSSIBLE!
